entry.title: South Korea commits $1 trillion to expand memory chip production, build AI data centers, and commercialize humanoid robots by 2028 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: South Korea plans to invest $1 trillion by 2028 to expand its memory chip production, develop AI data centers, and commercialize humanoid robots. This initiative aims to strengthen the country's position in the global semiconductor market, support AI infrastructure, and advance physical AI technologies, including robotics for industrial use. The government and major tech companies like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Hyundai are leading these efforts to meet rising demand driven by the AI industry. The investment includes $585 billion for new chip fabrication plants to double DRAM production, $357 billion for AI data centers across various provinces, and significant funding to develop humanoid robots through Hyundai's partnership with Boston Dynamics. These projects require substantial energy and water resources, prompting plans to secure power from renewable and nuclear sources. However, the push for automation has sparked concerns among labor unions about job security, leading to potential strikes and public debate over the distribution of profits from the AI boom.

entry.title: Moondream details GPU bubble in AI model inference and introduces pipelined decoding to improve GPU utilization and reduce idle time [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Moondream's blog post explores the inefficiencies in GPU utilization during AI model inference, specifically addressing the issue known as the "GPU bubble," where GPUs remain idle while waiting for CPU instructions. The company introduces its inference engine, Photon, which uses a technique called pipelined decoding to overlap CPU and GPU tasks, significantly improving throughput and reducing idle time during token generation in language models. The article details how traditional sequential processing causes the GPU to wait for the CPU to complete housekeeping tasks between generating tokens, leading to underutilization. Photon overcomes this by launching GPU computations for the next token before the CPU finishes processing the previous one, using mechanisms like ping-pong buffer slots to manage memory safely and maintain continuous GPU operation. This approach allows Moondream to achieve near real-time inference speeds and up to 35% higher decoding throughput on NVIDIA hardware. The innovation highlights potential improvements in AI model efficiency by optimizing hardware coordination, which could influence future developments in AI inference engines and GPU utilization strategies.

entry.title: LongCat releases LongCat-2.0, a large-scale MoE model with 1.6 trillion parameters and 48 billion active parameters [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: LongCat has announced the release of LongCat-2.0, a large-scale mixture of experts (MoE) model featuring 1.6 trillion parameters, with 48 billion active parameters during operation. This development represents a significant advancement in scalable AI model architecture, aiming to enhance performance and efficiency in handling complex tasks. The model leverages a mixture of experts approach to activate only a subset of its parameters for each input, allowing it to maintain a massive overall size while managing computational resources effectively. This design enables LongCat-2.0 to deliver powerful capabilities without the proportional increase in processing demands typically associated with such large models.

entry.title: Ornith-1.0 launches self-improving open-source coding models with 9B to 397B parameters, featuring reinforcement learning and 256K token context windows [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Ornith-1.0 is a new open-source suite of self-improving coding models ranging from 9 billion to 397 billion parameters, designed to enhance agentic coding through reinforcement learning. These models, which include dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, achieve state-of-the-art performance on several coding benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-Bench. They feature a large 256K token context window and are licensed under MIT, making them freely accessible worldwide. The models are built on top of Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 and utilize a novel training framework that jointly optimizes solution generation and the scaffolding guiding those solutions, improving search trajectories and output quality. Ornith-1.0 supports multiple serving environments, including vLLM and SGLang, and offers compatibility with OpenAI-style tool calls and reasoning parsers, facilitating advanced reasoning and tool integration in coding tasks. Ornith-1.0's availability in various precision and format variants allows deployment on single or multi-GPU setups, with the smaller 9B model fitting on a single 80GB GPU and larger MoE models requiring distributed tensor parallelism. This release represents a significant advancement in open-source coding AI, providing powerful, scalable tools for developers and researchers.

entry.title: Developer uses AI assistance to diagnose and address parsing regression in hyperscript language, illustrating AI's strengths and limitations in debugging [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A developer detailed their experience using AI assistance to diagnose and address a parsing regression in the hyperscript language, highlighting both the strengths and limitations of AI in debugging complex code. The issue arose from a recent update that caused the parser to misinterpret certain expressions, and AI helped quickly identify the root cause related to grammar changes during refactoring. While AI was effective in pinpointing the problem, it was less successful in proposing a robust fix, offering solutions that were either too specific or introduced unnecessary complexity. This case illustrates the potential of AI as a valuable tool in software development, but also underscores the importance of human judgment to avoid overreliance and to implement appropriate solutions.

entry.title: Researchers present TraceRetain, a framework for selective memory retention in frozen LLM agents that improves task success and robustness under noisy conditions in ALFWorld benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced TraceRetain, a framework designed to enhance memory retention in frozen large language model (LLM) agents by selectively managing external memory based on features like success, age, and relevance. Tested on the ALFWorld benchmark with the gpt-5-mini model, TraceRetain demonstrated improved task success and robustness, particularly under noisy conditions where traditional memory approaches degraded significantly. The framework effectively maintains high task performance by evicting less useful memory entries, preventing memory pollution caused by distractors. In controlled experiments with synthetic noise, TraceRetain preserved task success rates and precision, outperforming unbounded memory and FIFO-based retention methods. Evaluations showed that memory-augmented policies solved more tasks compared to no-memory baselines, highlighting the benefits of bounded retention for efficiency without sacrificing accuracy. The study suggests that selective memory retention is especially valuable in environments with noisy data streams, offering a practical approach to improving long-horizon LLM agent performance.

entry.title: Researchers propose evidence-informed belief updates for large language models to improve continual scientific discovery by increasing non-stationary surprisal and reducing spurious rewards in hypothesis search [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have proposed a method to improve continual scientific discovery using large language models (LLMs) by updating their beliefs based on prior evidence. This approach addresses limitations in existing methods like AutoDiscovery, which treat surprisal-a measure of how surprising new information is-as static, whereas human reasoning considers surprisal relative to evolving beliefs. By incorporating evidence-informed belief updates, the researchers enable LLMs to compute non-stationary surprisal, better reflecting the dynamic nature of scientific inquiry. The study compares different belief-updating mechanisms and finds that embedding-based retrieval augmented generation over prior discoveries most effectively anticipates updated beliefs, identifying a significant portion of static surprisals as spurious. The researchers introduce belief-update filtering and diversity maximization to the hypothesis search process, which together increase accumulated non-stationary surprisal by over 30% across multiple discovery domains. This demonstrates that continual scientific discovery with LLMs benefits from both improved belief measurement and search strategies that reduce redundancy and promote diverse hypotheses.

entry.title: Researchers introduce EvalSafetyGap, a hybrid survey and conceptual framework analyzing LLM evaluation-safety failures across eight evidence streams from 2018 to 2026 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced EvalSafetyGap, a hybrid survey and conceptual framework designed to analyze failures in large language model (LLM) evaluation and AI safety from 2018 to 2026. This work addresses the challenge that improvements in benchmark scores and safety metrics may not accurately reflect the underlying safety properties they intend to measure. EvalSafetyGap synthesizes evidence across eight key areas, including benchmark validity, dynamic evaluation, and governance, and employs a structured audit of ten models to compare evaluation and alignment proxy failures under optimization pressure. The framework incorporates concepts such as Goodhart's Law, Instability Decomposition, and the Alignment Trilemma to facilitate testable comparisons. The audit reveals that the relationship between model capability and adversarial robustness is statistically inconclusive, with governance and disclosure playing a larger role in the observed safety gaps than behavioral robustness. Due to heterogeneous evaluation protocols, the audit serves as a diagnostic tool rather than a ranking system. This contribution provides a shared vocabulary and evidence map to support more transparent, dynamic, and auditable approaches to LLM safety evaluation and alignment practices.

entry.title: Researchers introduce PixelRAG, a retrieval-augmented generation method using web page screenshots in pixel space, outperforming text-based baselines on Wikipedia and open-domain QA tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed PixelRAG, a novel retrieval-augmented generation method that processes web pages as pixel-based screenshots rather than text. This approach preserves the visual layout and formatting of websites, enabling an end-to-end system that retrieves and reads information directly from images. PixelRAG operates on a large-scale dataset of 30 million Wikipedia screenshots and outperforms traditional text-based retrieval methods on various question-answering benchmarks, including text-centric and multimodal tasks. Built on a visual embedding model fine-tuned with contrastive training on screenshot data, PixelRAG feeds retrieved images directly into a vision-language model without converting them to text. This method not only improves accuracy by up to 18.1% over text-based baselines but also offers efficiency gains through image compression, reducing token costs by up to three times while maintaining performance. The findings suggest that web retrieval can be effectively conducted in the web's native visual form, challenging the conventional reliance on text representations.

entry.title: Researchers propose LoRA-tuned large language model using multi-view speech features for dementia detection, achieving 90.14% F1-score on ADReSSo dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a low-rank adaptation (LoRA)-tuned large language model (LLM) that integrates multiple speech-derived features to detect dementia with high accuracy. By combining automatic speech recognition transcripts with pause markers, discourse-level topic cues, temporal fluency statistics, and phonological sequences into a unified prompt, the model achieves a 90.14% F1-score on the ADReSSo dataset without relying on separate modality-specific encoders or late-stage fusion. This approach addresses limitations of previous methods that focused on single speech representations by enabling structured multi-view reasoning within a single LLM. Ablation studies confirm that each speech-derived feature contributes complementarily to the model's performance, highlighting the benefit of integrating diverse speech signals for early, non-invasive dementia screening.

entry.title: Researchers propose an agentic AI pipeline combining deep forecasting, anomaly detection, and LLM reasoning for appliance-level energy anomaly detection and maintenance recommendations in office buildings [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed an integrated AI pipeline that enhances appliance-level energy anomaly detection and maintenance recommendations in office buildings. The system combines deep time-series forecasting, variational anomaly detection, and large language model (LLM) reasoning to provide prioritized, actionable insights for facility managers. It monitors seven office appliances using a hybrid forecasting model and flags abnormal energy consumption with a variational autoencoder, while a multi-stage LangChain pipeline generates structured diagnoses and human-readable reports, incorporating operator feedback through a reflective memory layer.

entry.title: Researchers propose SCSuff metric to evaluate sufficiency of large language model explanations based on models' own input beliefs, finding explanations generally insufficient and weakly correlated with size or accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced a new metric called SCSuff to evaluate the sufficiency of free-text explanations provided by large language models (LLMs). This metric assesses whether explanations contain enough information to justify the model's output by using the model itself to generate alternative inputs based on its explanations, reflecting the model's own beliefs. Their findings indicate that LLM explanations are generally insufficient and show only weak correlations with model size, accuracy, or output entropy. The study extends the concept of sufficiency from feature attributions to arbitrary explanations and highlights that explanation sufficiency depends on the input distribution, which must be explicitly defined. Experiments demonstrate that SCSuff aligns with targeted perturbation tests and that the metric can be predicted from internal model representations, suggesting its potential to guide the detection and improvement of explanation quality in LLMs.

entry.title: Researchers identify modal and correlation ceilings in test-time scaling for language models, showing extra sampling can worsen answers and increase costs beyond a few dozen draws [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have identified limits in the effectiveness of test-time scaling for language models, showing that sampling more than a few dozen times can actually degrade answer quality and increase computational costs. While drawing more samples initially raises the chance of generating a correct answer, the ability to select the right one plateaus early, creating an "identifiability gap" where additional samples do not improve final selection and may reinforce confident errors. The study introduces the concepts of the modal ceiling and correlation ceiling, which mark the points beyond which extra sampling yields no benefit for answer selection or benchmark scoring, respectively. The authors propose a metric called the effective number of samples to quantify this cutoff, emphasizing that the main challenge lies in recognizing the correct answer rather than generating it. This insight suggests that language model systems should limit sampling to optimize performance and resource use.

entry.title: Researchers find clinical evidence strength is encoded in language model representations but not reflected in their stated evidence grades across 22 models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers analyzed 22 large language models (LLMs) to determine if these models encode the strength of clinical evidence in their internal representations and whether they explicitly convey this information when summarizing clinical claims. Using a dataset of over 45,000 clinical claims harmonized into a four-level evidence grading system, the study found that while a linear estimator could reliably recover evidence strength from the models' activations, the models themselves rarely stated accurate evidence grades. This discrepancy suggests that LLMs carry an implicit signal about evidence strength that is not reflected in their explicit outputs. The study tested models ranging from 0.6 to 70 billion parameters, including general, medical, and reasoning-focused LLMs, and found that the recoverable evidence strength signal was largely lexical and distinct from factual truth. However, this signal did not generalize well across different topics or grading frameworks. Despite this, the models could still weakly identify claims with weak support. These findings highlight a gap between the internal knowledge of clinical LLMs and their communicated confidence, indicating that current models do not effectively express the strength of evidence in their summaries.

entry.title: Study compares affective cues in embeddings from 12 text encoders across three psychological emotion theories, finding instruction-aware open-weight models capture strong word-level affective information while proprietary models excel at sentence-level tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study evaluated the affective information captured by embeddings from twelve recent text encoders across three psychological emotion theories, using both word- and sentence-level data. The research found that instruction-aware open-weight models contain as much or more word-level affective information compared to proprietary models, while proprietary and task-tuned encoders perform better on sentence-level affective classification tasks. The study also applied a semantic data-leakage prevention technique to enhance robustness and included a qualitative analysis of the affective cues encoded in the latent representations.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Symbolic Mechanistic Data Attribution to trace training data influence on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct's behavioral policies, revealing safety gaps and feature interference in 200 fine-tuning pairs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Symbolic Mechanistic Data Attribution (SMDA), a new framework that links training data to the interpretable symbolic policies guiding a model's behavior. Applying SMDA to Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct, they analyzed 200 supervised fine-tuning pairs to trace how each example influences the model's refusal behavior, revealing safety gaps and feature interference in the training process. SMDA uses Ridge regression over sparse autoencoder features to model target behaviors and decomposes the impact of training examples through feature activation and output probability pathways. This approach uncovers systematic weaknesses in the base model's safety responses, explains differing influences of harmful versus harmless training pairs, and identifies cases where training data affects unintended features. By combining mechanistic interpretability with data attribution, SMDA offers a more detailed and scalable diagnostic tool than existing black-box influence methods or manual circuit analysis, enhancing understanding of how training data shapes high-level model decisions.

entry.title: Researchers identify intervention bias in zero-shot LLM educational advisors and demonstrate supervised policy learning eliminates bias with near-zero calibration error on Open University dataset [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have identified a previously unquantified issue called intervention bias in zero-shot large language model (LLM) educational advisors, where these models recommend interventions even when an optimal oracle policy suggests no action is needed. In a study using the Open University Learning Analytics Dataset, zero-shot GPT-4o showed a high false-positive rate, recommending unnecessary actions for 73% of students at a key checkpoint, compared to the oracle's 29.9%. Similar miscalibration was observed in commercial retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and SQL-augmented retrieval systems. The study demonstrates that supervised policy learning methods, including a trajectory-conditioned Decision Transformer and an XGBoost classifier trained on oracle-labeled data, effectively eliminate this bias, achieving near-zero calibration error and high predictive accuracy across multiple action classes. These supervised models operate with low latency and maintain decision consistency, highlighting their potential for more reliable educational advisory systems. Additionally, the researchers reveal an evaluation gap where LLM-based scoring methods fail to detect intervention bias, often favoring fluent but excessive recommendations over decision quality. The findings emphasize the importance of task-specific training and careful evaluation to improve the reliability of AI-driven educational interventions.

entry.title: Researchers evaluate five defense methods against five attack types on seven instruction-tuned LLMs, finding prompt-time activation defenses blind to prefilling attacks and introducing response-time probing that eliminates prefilling success [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers conducted a systematic evaluation of five defense methods against five types of attacks on seven instruction-tuned large language models ranging from 7 to 31 billion parameters. They found that prompt-time activation defenses are inherently ineffective against prefilling attacks, with some methods like AlphaSteer showing zero success against certain attacks but only 50% effectiveness against prefilling. To address this, the team introduced response-time probing, a technique that analyzes the model's hidden states during the first generated tokens, achieving near-perfect detection and eliminating prefilling attack success without false positives. The study demonstrated that defenses relying on gating interventions based on a single layer's activation alignment are vulnerable to attacks that craft activations within the benign reference space. By combining response-time probing with existing methods like AlphaSteer's null-space steering, the researchers achieved high overall defense success, effectively countering both prefilling and semantic attacks. They also highlighted limitations in current evaluation metrics and showed that diverse negative training data significantly reduce false positives. The researchers have released their code, attack implementations, and evaluation data to support further study.

entry.title: Researchers introduce LLM4MOF, a closed-loop framework using large language model agents for interpretable inverse design and simulation of metal-organic frameworks across multiple tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed LLM4MOF, a closed-loop framework that uses large language model agents to design and simulate metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) across multiple tasks. This system autonomously generates interpretable design hypotheses about metal nodes, linkers, pore geometry, and functional chemistry, then translates these into constraints to select candidate MOFs. Through iterative testing and simulation, LLM4MOF refines its designs, focusing on top-performing structures without prior knowledge of the global property landscape. LLM4MOF evaluates hypotheses using diagnostic tests that isolate the effects of geometry, chemistry, and metal choice on performance. It efficiently explores six adsorption, separation, and electronic-structure tasks within 400 property evaluations, outperforming random search and genetic algorithms. The framework also generates new MOFs de novo and adapts their geometry to specific conditions during live simulation, demonstrating that language-model agents can conduct interpretable, simulation-based inverse design without needing to train separate models for each objective.

entry.title: Researchers introduce a failure-driven evolution framework enabling a meta-agent to adaptively coordinate diverse retrievers for multimodal document reasoning, achieving up to 19.6-point gains on MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a failure-driven evolution framework that enables a meta-agent to adaptively coordinate various retrievers-lexical, semantic, and multimodal-for multimodal document reasoning. This approach transforms retrieval from a fixed initial step into an adaptive, step-wise decision process during multi-step document question answering, leading to significant performance improvements. The evolved agent achieved up to 19.6-point gains on benchmarks like MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench, outperforming recent systems such as MACT, MDocAgent, and SimpleDoc. The meta-agent autonomously analyzes incorrect reasoning paths, probes the environment to identify root causes, and iteratively refines the task agent's instructions. This process allows the agent to learn when and how to invoke different retrievers and effectively combine evidence across modalities and pages. Detailed analyses show that the improvements stem from adaptive routing and evidence composition rather than fixed retrieval strategies, highlighting a shift from narrow lexical methods to rich multi-tool coordination. These findings suggest that autonomous multi-agent coordination offers a promising new paradigm for multimodal document reasoning, enabling more flexible and effective retrieval orchestration tailored to the demands of individual reasoning steps.

entry.title: Researchers introduce ARMOR, an adaptive retriever optimization method improving low-resource telecom question answering by enhancing retrieval and generation in domain-specific benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed ARMOR, an adaptive retriever optimization method designed to enhance question answering (QA) in the telecom domain, particularly in low-resource settings. ARMOR improves retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by focusing on query-side retriever adaptation rather than generator fine-tuning, which can lead to over-specialization. The method jointly optimizes two objectives-the latent-document RAG likelihood and the InfoNCE contrastive objective-to better support evidence retrieval and answer generation across telecom-specific benchmarks. ARMOR works by learning separate temperature parameters for the RAG retrieval distribution and the InfoNCE softmax, while regularizing the adapted query encoder toward a frozen base encoder. This approach addresses the fragmented and technical nature of telecom data, which includes standards, papers, and specialized protocol language. Evaluations demonstrate that ARMOR enhances both retrieval accuracy and generative QA performance in several in-domain scenarios, offering a promising solution for improving domain-specific QA systems with limited resources.

entry.title: Researchers present SEVA, a self-evolving verification agent using process rewards to improve fact attribution and produce auditable, structured outputs with multi-round self-refinement [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SEVA, a self-evolving verification agent designed to improve fact attribution in large language models by producing structured, auditable outputs and enabling multi-round self-refinement. Unlike traditional verifiers that provide only binary labels, SEVA offers detailed evidence alignments, reasoning chains, calibrated confidence scores, and a six-category error diagnosis with actionable fixes, enhancing both agent self-correction and operator auditing. Training SEVA with reinforcement learning posed challenges due to the complexity of its multi-component outputs, which standard binary rewards could not effectively handle. The team addressed this by introducing a process reward that breaks down verification quality into five components, restoring training gradients and enabling a curriculum where the agent first masters verification behavior before improving outcomes. This approach also revealed that repeated self-refinement rounds produce benchmark-specific specialists rather than generalists. SEVA's 3-billion-parameter model matches the performance of GPT-4o-mini on the ClearFacts benchmark while delivering richer, more transparent verification results, highlighting the importance of aligning reward granularity with output complexity in reinforcement learning tasks.

entry.title: Researchers propose MATCH, a scalable framework that enhances sparse attention in long-context transformers with dynamic in-context retrieval, improving performance on synthetic and real-world language tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced MATCH, a new framework designed to improve the efficiency and scalability of large language models (LLMs) in handling long-context scenarios. MATCH enhances sparse attention mechanisms by dynamically integrating in-context information through an efficient retrieval system, addressing the limitations of traditional attention methods that suffer from high computational costs and performance drops in long-range recall tasks. The framework avoids rigid structural constraints like local attention windows, which often degrade performance, by augmenting sparsified attention with dynamic retrieval. Empirical tests demonstrate that MATCH significantly boosts the performance of sparse-attention models on both synthetic benchmarks and real-world natural language tasks, making it a versatile solution for improving in-context retrieval while maintaining computational efficiency.

entry.title: Researchers introduce SABER-Math, an automated benchmark for evaluating mathematical information retrieval using 283K high-school math problems and LLM-based relevance ratings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SABER-Math, the first fully automated benchmark designed to evaluate mathematical information retrieval (IR) systems without requiring expert annotations. Utilizing a dataset of 283,000 high-school-level math problems and solutions, SABER-Math creates reranking tasks by extracting solution summaries and topics with large language models (LLMs), identifying relevant documents through topic and lexical similarities, and generating fine-grained relevance ratings via an LLM-based preference tournament. This benchmark addresses the challenge of assessing IR systems' effectiveness in mathematical contexts, where existing benchmarks often fail to capture nuanced relevance. The study evaluated various retrieval methods, including lexical retrievers, specialized math retrieval systems, and modern embedding models. Results showed that while embedding models outperform traditional and math-specific baselines, they still face difficulties in symbol-intensive areas such as Algebra and Calculus. Additionally, the research highlights that general-purpose IR benchmarks like MTEB do not reliably predict performance in mathematical retrieval tasks, underscoring the importance of math-specific evaluation tools like SABER-Math.

entry.title: Researchers analyze non-sequential multimodal sentence embeddings in the SONAR model, identifying sensitive dimensions as anomaly detectors and exploring correction methods to improve multimodal representation reliability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers conducted a detailed study of non-sequential multimodal sentence embeddings, focusing on the SONAR model. They found that certain embedding dimensions are particularly sensitive to perturbations and can effectively detect decoding anomalies. By examining the consistency between encoding and decoding processes, they developed an accurate anomaly detector and explored methods to adjust specific embedding dimensions to correct errors. This analysis highlights the importance of understanding the internal structure of embeddings to improve the reliability of multimodal representations. The findings suggest that targeted modifications to sensitive dimensions can enhance the robustness of models that integrate multiple data modalities.

entry.title: Researchers propose permutation-invariant fine-tuning for structured metadata retrieval to reduce field order impact, improving search accuracy across 15 languages with a new benchmark and models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have identified that the order of fields in structured metadata records significantly affects retrieval quality when using text encoders fine-tuned for search tasks. They propose a permutation-invariant fine-tuning method (PI-FT) that randomizes field order and applies field dropout during training, ensuring the model learns to associate meaning with field labels rather than their positions. This approach reduces the retrieval performance drop caused by changes in field order from 7.4 to 0.2 nDCG@10 points with minimal impact on accuracy. The study focuses on a catalog of nearly 10,000 development indicators searchable in 15 languages, introducing DevDataBench, a benchmark of queries generated by large language models to cover all indicators for training and evaluation. A fine-tuned 118M-parameter encoder using PI-FT outperforms zero-shot baselines, especially in low-resource languages. The researchers have released the benchmark, models, and a reusable PI-FT framework to support improved and robust metadata retrieval across languages.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini that generates and refines novel scientific hypotheses, validated in biomedical applications including drug repurposing for acute myeloid leukemia [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Co-Scientist, a multi-agent AI system built on the Gemini platform designed to generate and refine novel scientific hypotheses. This system supports scientists by formulating new research hypotheses based on their objectives and existing scientific evidence, with a focus on accelerating discovery through continuous hypothesis generation, critique, and refinement. Co-Scientist's architecture includes an asynchronous task execution framework and a tournament evolution process that improves hypothesis quality over time. The system has been validated in biomedical applications such as drug repurposing, novel target discovery, and understanding antimicrobial resistance mechanisms. Notably, Co-Scientist identified new drug repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukemia, which were confirmed through in vitro experiments. These results demonstrate Co-Scientist's potential to enhance scientific discovery and support AI-empowered research efforts.

entry.title: Researchers propose distributionally robust reinforcement learning from human feedback to improve large language model fine-tuning and out-of-distribution task performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a distributionally robust reinforcement learning approach from human feedback (RLHF) to enhance the fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) and improve their performance on tasks that differ from the training data. This method aims to maintain model effectiveness even when the prompt distribution during deployment varies significantly from that seen during fine-tuning. The team formulated distributionally robust optimization versions of two common fine-tuning techniques-reward-based RLHF and reward-free direct preference optimization (DPO)-and proposed minibatch gradient descent algorithms with proven convergence guarantees. The researchers evaluated their approach by training models on the Unified-Feedback dataset and testing them on out-of-distribution tasks across different datasets. Results demonstrated that the robust training improved the accuracy of learned reward models overall, with notable gains in reasoning tasks. Additionally, the robust policy optimization methods showed enhanced performance on out-of-distribution tasks, suggesting that this approach can make LLM fine-tuning more reliable across diverse applications.

entry.title: Researchers develop post-training fine-tuning method to improve large language models' convention formation and communication efficiency, validated on two new benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a post-training fine-tuning method to enhance large language models' ability to form ad-hoc conventions and communicate more efficiently in multi-turn interactions. This approach targets demonstrations of convention formation identified through heuristics and has been validated using two newly designed benchmarks that focus on this capability. The first benchmark is a cognitively motivated interaction task that reliably elicits convention formation trends observed in humans, while the second is a document-grounded reference completion task reflecting real-world convention formation behavior. The studies demonstrate that language models subjected to this post-training process show significant improvements in their convention formation abilities across both evaluation methods.

entry.title: Researchers train small attention-only transformers achieving perfect indirect object identification with minimal circuits specialized into additive and contrastive subcircuits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have trained small, attention-only transformer models from scratch to perform the Indirect Object Identification (IOI) task, achieving perfect accuracy with minimal architecture. A single-layer model with just two attention heads, lacking multilayer perceptrons and normalization layers, successfully resolves IOI by specializing its heads into additive and contrastive subcircuits. This demonstrates that task-specific training can produce highly interpretable and minimal computational circuits within transformers. The study employed techniques such as residual stream decomposition, spectral analysis, and embedding interventions to analyze how these attention heads function. Additionally, a two-layer, one-head model was shown to integrate information primarily through query-key interactions, highlighting the simplicity of the mechanisms involved. These findings provide a controlled framework for understanding the computational foundations of transformer reasoning and contribute to the field of mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Value-Action Alignment Rate to assess privacy and prosocial value conflicts in large language models' data-sharing decisions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new method called the Value-Action Alignment Rate (VAAR) to evaluate how large language models (LLMs) handle conflicts between privacy concerns and prosocial motivations in decisions about personal data sharing. This approach uses a context-based protocol that sequentially assesses privacy attitudes, prosocialness, and willingness to share data within a single session, allowing for a more integrated understanding of the models' decision-making processes. By applying multi-group structural equation modeling, the study identifies how these competing values influence data-sharing actions across different LLMs. The research reveals that while LLMs exhibit stable but distinct profiles regarding privacy and prosocial attitudes, there is significant variation in how well their expressed values align with their data-sharing behaviors. This finding highlights the complexity of modeling human-like value-driven decisions in AI systems and provides a framework for more nuanced assessments of ethical considerations in AI data handling.

entry.title: Researchers introduce MLCL benchmark to evaluate multilingual tool calling in large language models, finding parameter value language mismatch causes execution errors across Chinese, Hindi, and Igbo [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced MLCL, a new benchmark designed to evaluate the robustness of multilingual tool calling in large language models (LLMs). Their study focuses on Chinese, Hindi, and the low-resource language Igbo, revealing that many execution errors occur despite correct understanding and tool selection. A key issue identified is the mismatch between the language of parameter values generated by the models and the language-invariant conventions required for execution, leading to failures.

entry.title: Researchers propose a longitudinal NLP modeling and evaluation paradigm for behavioral sequences, updating pipeline components and demonstrating improved accuracy on 17k diary transcripts with PTSD data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have proposed a new longitudinal modeling and evaluation framework for natural language processing (NLP) that addresses the limitations of treating documents as independent and unordered samples. This approach updates key components of the NLP pipeline, including evaluation splits that consider generalization across individuals and time, accuracy metrics that distinguish between-person differences from within-person dynamics, sequence inputs that incorporate historical context, and model structures that capture varying levels of latent state detail over time. The framework was tested on a dataset of 17,000 daily diary transcripts linked to PTSD symptom severity from 238 participants, revealing that traditional document-level evaluations can produce significantly different and sometimes opposite conclusions compared to this more ecologically valid method. The study highlights the importance of shifting from conventional word-sequence evaluations toward behavior-sequence paradigms in NLP, especially for longitudinal data where documents are nested within individuals and ordered chronologically. By incorporating temporal and individual-specific factors, the proposed paradigm offers improved accuracy and more meaningful insights into behavioral sequences captured through language.

entry.title: Researchers introduce a test-time detoxification method for large language models using zeroth-order optimization to reduce toxic outputs without retraining or learning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a test-time detoxification method for large language models that reduces toxic or inappropriate outputs without requiring retraining or additional learning. This approach uses zeroth-order optimization to approximate the gradient of toxicity relative to input embeddings and applies a few descent steps to guide the model toward generating less harmful text. The method only needs access to input embeddings, a toxicity scoring function, and forward model evaluations, making it applicable even in black-box settings. The technique has demonstrated robust reductions in toxicity across various models and prompts while maintaining a favorable balance between toxicity reduction and generation quality. By treating word embeddings as control variables, this work promotes the use of black-box optimization to enhance the safety and scalability of autoregressive language models without needing access to internal model computations or retraining.

entry.title: Researchers propose Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding to improve structured output accuracy in large language models by up to 24 percentage points without additional training [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding (DCCD), a two-step, training-free method designed to improve the accuracy of structured outputs generated by large language models (LLMs). This approach first produces an unconstrained draft and then applies constrained decoding conditioned on this draft to ensure syntactic validity, addressing issues where traditional constrained decoding can lead to semantically incorrect outputs despite being locally valid. DCCD has demonstrated improvements in strict structured accuracy by up to 24 percentage points on benchmarks like GSM8K, enabling smaller models to perform comparably to larger constrained models and enhancing parameter efficiency. The method works by separating semantic planning from structural enforcement, which reduces the distortion caused by hard constraints during decoding. Analysis through a KL-projection framework shows that draft conditioning increases the feasible output space and lowers the cumulative penalty imposed by constraints. This technique can also incorporate a best-of-K draft selection to further enhance performance across various structured reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Researchers localize and analyze policy routing circuits in alignment-trained language models from 2B to 72B parameters, revealing gating mechanisms that control refusal and safety behaviors [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have identified and analyzed the policy routing circuits in alignment-trained language models ranging from 2 billion to 72 billion parameters. They discovered an intermediate-layer attention gate that detects content and activates deeper amplifier heads to enforce refusal behaviors. This gating mechanism, though contributing less than 1% of output, is causally necessary for controlling model responses, including refusal and safety behaviors, and is consistent across multiple models from different labs. The study reveals that in smaller models, the gate and amplifier are single attention heads, while in larger models they form bands across layers. The gating mechanism operates early in the processing pipeline and modulates responses from refusal to factual answering. The researchers also demonstrated that safety behaviors are controlled by routing rather than removal, and that the circuit's location can shift across model generations without changing overall behavior. They introduced novel methods such as interchange testing and cipher contrast analysis to reliably identify and map these circuits, showing that any encoding that bypasses detection-layer pattern matching can circumvent policy enforcement regardless of deeper layer processing.

entry.title: Researchers propose Evidence Graph Consistency framework for hallucination detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, revealing model-dependent patterns across six large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced the Evidence Graph Consistency (EGC) framework to detect hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems used by large language models. Unlike previous methods that rely on simple similarity measures, EGC constructs a local evidence graph for each response and evaluates structural consistency to identify hallucinations. Testing across six large language models with over 5,700 responses revealed that EGC's effectiveness varies by model family, showing expected results for Llama-2 models but opposite patterns for GPT-4, GPT-3.5, and Mistral-7B. This finding indicates that hallucination patterns differ qualitatively among model families, suggesting that embedding-based graph consistency measures cannot universally detect hallucinations across all models. The study highlights the need for model-specific approaches in hallucination detection within RAG frameworks.

entry.title: Researchers quantify subliminal behavioral transfer ratios in language model distillation using Llama-2 and Qwen2.5 teacher models evaluated on JailbreakBench prompts with GPT-4.1 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have quantified the subliminal transfer of undesirable behaviors during language model distillation, a process where a student model inherits traits from a teacher model. Using Llama-2-7B-Chat and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as teacher models, they varied steering strengths and distilled student models with only benign data. Evaluation on 100 JailbreakBench prompts by GPT-4.1 revealed that while subliminal transfer is robust, it exhibits different scaling patterns between the two models, with Llama-2 showing a sharp threshold and Qwen2.5 demonstrating continuous and higher levels of transfer. This study provides the first systematic quantification of subliminal behavioral transfer ratios, highlighting that undesirable characteristics can persist even when distillation is guided by benign data. The findings emphasize the need to consider such transfer effects in model distillation to ensure safer and more reliable language models.

entry.title: Researchers find that lossy memory in language models leads to worse performance than empty memory, with brittle memory causing confident but incorrect answers across eight models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have found that language models with lossy memory-memories that retain incorrect conclusions but lose the supporting reasoning-perform worse than models with no memory at all. This phenomenon, termed brittle memory, causes models to confidently provide wrong answers instead of abstaining. The study evaluated eight models using a method called reclaim evaluation, which compresses interactions and tests if corrections can recover accurate answers, revealing that lossy memory consistently underperforms compared to empty memory, especially in models inclined to answer rather than abstain. The researchers demonstrated that preserving the original source information while discarding derived conclusions improves the model's ability to correct errors without increasing memory usage. This approach was effective across different models and real dialogue scenarios, such as the MultiWOZ dataset. The study also identified a boundary where this fix fails unless completeness is explicitly recorded. The work provides a controlled, judge-free evaluation framework and releases tools for further research on memory mechanisms in language models.

entry.title: Researchers introduce CARVE, a content-aware recurrent model improving linear attention efficiency and performance on reasoning benchmarks with lower memory and parameter use [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed CARVE, a content-aware recurrent model that enhances the efficiency and performance of linear attention mechanisms in neural networks. CARVE addresses key limitations in previous architectures by implementing an erase gate that considers stored memory content, improving parameter efficiency and enabling a mathematically valid triangular chunk solver for recurrent training. This approach leads to better performance on language modeling and reasoning benchmarks while reducing memory usage and parameter count. CARVE operates by erasing only along the key axis and reuses existing recurrent output tensors as signals for gating, replacing complex per-value projections with simpler scalar values per head. When trained on a large dataset with 1.3 billion parameters, CARVE achieved lower perplexity on WikiText and outperformed other recurrent models on multiple common-sense reasoning and retrieval tasks. The model also demonstrates improved computational efficiency with minimal throughput overhead and reduced peak memory consumption. The development of CARVE is supported by formal theoretical results covering aspects such as memory capacity, stability, gradient flow, and optimal chunk size, highlighting its potential as a more effective and resource-efficient alternative to existing recurrent architectures in natural language processing.

entry.title: Researchers propose Flexformer, a flexible linear Transformer with learnable attention kernels using trainable spectral frequencies, achieving improved efficiency and performance on long-sequence tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Flexformer, a flexible linear Transformer model that improves efficiency and performance on long-sequence tasks by learning attention kernels through trainable spectral frequencies. Unlike traditional Transformer models that face quadratic complexity due to their attention mechanisms, Flexformer uses a data-driven approach based on random Fourier features to enable a broader and more expressive family of attention kernels. The model includes both stationary and nonstationary variants, with the latter providing greater expressiveness. Extensive experiments in language modeling and sequence classification show that Flexformer consistently outperforms existing baselines. Additionally, it can be distilled from pretrained Transformers to approximate softmax attention and demonstrates strong kernel transferability across different domains, making it both efficient and competitive for handling long sequences.

entry.title: Researchers present Pepti-drift, a toxicity-aware framework for antigen-conditioned peptide generation that balances binding affinity and toxicity avoidance with improved speed and diversity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Pepti-drift, a novel framework for generating antigen-specific peptides that balances binding affinity with toxicity avoidance. This approach uses a toxicity-aware latent refinement process that guides peptide candidates toward effective binding while steering them away from toxic regions in peptide representation space. Pepti-drift addresses the challenge of overlapping features between binding and toxicity by employing a warm-up strategy that first focuses on binding attraction before increasing toxicity repulsion. Pepti-drift operates significantly faster than existing methods, achieving a 16.2-fold speed increase over PepMLM and a 1,092-fold increase over PepTune. The generated peptides demonstrate high validity, uniqueness, and sequence diversity, with reduced toxicity and hemolysis risk across various peptide lengths. This framework offers a scalable and controllable solution for designing safe and active antigen-specific peptides, advancing therapeutic peptide discovery.

entry.title: Researchers introduce GPTNT benchmark for real-time collaboration between multimodal AI agents in Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, revealing current models fail to defuse bombs under time pressure [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced GPTNT, a new benchmark designed to evaluate real-time collaboration between multimodal AI agents using the cooperative video game Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. In this setup, two agents must work together under time pressure to defuse bombs: one can see and manipulate the bomb but lacks instructions, while the other has the instructions but cannot interact with the bomb. Success requires effective communication and asynchronous action, highlighting challenges not captured by existing benchmarks. The GPTNT benchmark isolates collaboration from memorized knowledge by withholding the instruction manual, the partner, or both, testing what models can infer in real time. Experiments reveal that current state-of-the-art AI models fail to defuse any bombs under these conditions, unlike human players. The study identifies key weaknesses in state tracking, handling ambiguity, efficient decision-making under time constraints, and error recovery. By running on the actual game with procedurally generated puzzles and an active modding community, GPTNT offers a dynamic and evolving platform to measure collaborative AI performance beyond traditional evaluations. This benchmark aims to drive improvements in AI systems' ability to collaborate effectively in complex, time-sensitive tasks.

entry.title: Researchers develop self-supervised AI agent that discovers tens of thousands of theorems from axioms alone in a formal system, improving large language model proof performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a self-supervised AI agent capable of autonomously discovering tens of thousands of theorems within a formal axiomatic system, starting solely from axioms and inference rules. This agent builds a growing library of useful theorems by alternating between proof search and theorem extraction, which it then reuses as lemmas to facilitate further proofs. The discoveries include theorems that are meaningful from a human mathematical perspective and improve the proof performance of large language models (LLMs) when used as prompt lemmas. The study demonstrates that useful theorems can emerge from automated proof search without relying on pre-existing human theorem libraries. This approach suggests a promising direction toward self-evolving AI systems in mathematics, whose findings remain formally verifiable and can enhance the reasoning capabilities of existing AI models.

entry.title: Researchers introduce MedEvoEval, a longitudinal evaluation framework for doctor agents evolving through simulated outpatient clinical episodes with 700 processed cases and detailed action traces [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed MedEvoEval, a new longitudinal evaluation framework designed to assess the evolving performance of doctor agents through simulated outpatient clinical episodes. This framework captures detailed action traces across 700 processed cases, allowing for the analysis of how these agents acquire evidence, utilize resources, and make diagnostic and management decisions over time. MedEvoEval addresses limitations of existing medical QA benchmarks by focusing on episode-level decisions and cross-episode learning, providing a more comprehensive evaluation of clinical decision systems. MedEvoEval converts each case into role-specific views and reveals evidence only through valid actions, recording structured traces that link observations, actions, outputs, and scores. The released artifact includes an episode runner, scoring scripts, and analysis tools. Experiments demonstrate that this approach uncovers process costs not visible in final-answer scoring, highlights resource allocation in multidisciplinary consultations, and supports analyses of memory development, transfer learning, and retention in doctor agents. This framework offers a concrete basis for evaluating whether doctor agents improve through experience, transfer useful behaviors, and maintain earlier capabilities, advancing the development of adaptive clinical decision systems.

entry.title: Researchers evaluate zero-shot localized concept naming with mid-scale multimodal large language models, achieving 62%-88% accuracy and proposing a reproducible low-cost C-XAI framework [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have evaluated the ability of mid-scale Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to perform zero-shot localized concept naming by labeling bounding-box regions at both object and part levels. Their study introduced a reproducible zero-shot evaluation protocol for Concept Naming (CoNa), including category-constrained prompting for moderate vocabularies and an embedding-similarity-based approach for larger label sets. Experiments with four MLLMs demonstrated consistent performance across datasets, achieving 62% to 88% exact-match accuracy at the object level, indicating the potential for training-free concept annotation from localized image regions. The researchers also discussed the limitations and failure modes of these models and released a reproducible framework to facilitate future low-cost concept-based Explainable AI (C-XAI) research. This work addresses the challenge of limited fine-grained concept annotations and offers a practical approach to generating human-understandable explanations grounded in semantic concepts without additional training.

entry.title: Researchers introduce PolicyGuard, a dialogue-grounded sub-agent verifier that improves policy adherence in LLM agents by reasoning over full conversation context and providing actionable feedback [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed PolicyGuard, a dialogue-grounded sub-agent verifier designed to enhance policy adherence in large language model (LLM) agents. Unlike previous approaches that rely on external safeguards to block non-compliant actions, PolicyGuard integrates full conversation context, self-reasoning over policies, and provides actionable feedback to guide the agent's next steps, addressing the complexities of multi-turn workflows and dialogue content. PolicyGuard was tested across multiple LLM vendors on the tau^2-BENCH airline dataset, showing significant improvements in policy adherence metrics while reducing unnecessary blocking compared to argument-level guards. This approach demonstrates a more nuanced and effective method for ensuring that LLM agents comply with organizational policies during interactive tasks.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Complexity Ceiling Benchmark to evaluate sequential reasoning decay in language models across three domains and varying task depths up to 50 steps [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed the Complexity Ceiling Benchmark (CCB) to systematically evaluate how the reasoning ability of language models declines as the number of sequential reasoning steps increases. The benchmark tests models across three distinct domains-grounded spatial state-tracking, abstract symbolic pointer manipulation, and transitive relational inference-varying task depth from 5 to 50 steps. Results from 6,000 trials involving five leading language models reveal a consistent geometric decay in reasoning performance, with models maintaining high accuracy in the first two domains even at 50 steps, but all models showing significant collapse by 5 steps in the third domain. The study also introduces a trace-level metric indicating that 14.5% of correct answers are achieved despite incorrect intermediate reasoning. Attempts to improve performance through forced verbose state-tracking did not raise the reasoning ceiling. Additionally, the step at which a model's reasoning first diverges proved to be a better predictor of accuracy within a domain than model size. Together, CCB and the geometric decay model provide a concise, interpretable measure of a model's long-horizon reasoning capabilities across different task families.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Hierarchical Experimentalist Agents (HExA), a training-free framework that improves large language model performance on complex physics tasks through active experimentation and skill reuse, achieving up to 77% success on the Interphyre benchmark [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Hierarchical Experimentalist Agents (HExA), a novel, training-free framework that enhances large language models' ability to solve complex physics problems through active experimentation and skill reuse. HExA iteratively designs experiments, learns reusable skills, and integrates experimental results to improve performance without requiring additional training data or supervision. Tested on the Interphyre benchmark, which simulates physical interventions, HExA significantly outperformed existing models, achieving up to 77% success compared to 2% by a baseline model. The framework operates by proposing and refining experiments relevant to specific queries, building a library of composable skills transferable across tasks. Unlike traditional approaches relying on fixed knowledge or retrieval, HExA adapts through active learning in novel domains. It also demonstrated strong generalization by achieving 44% success using skills learned from simpler tasks without further experimentation. This approach highlights the potential of active experimentation to enable language models to acquire practical knowledge and tackle long-horizon, complex tasks more effectively.

entry.title: Researchers propose Mixture of Debaters framework for dynamic multi-agent reasoning within a single model, achieving 3.7x lower latency and 87% token reduction on multimodal benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced the Mixture of Debaters (MoD), a novel framework that enables dynamic multi-agent reasoning within a single model by using the Mixture-of-Experts approach. This method overcomes limitations of existing debate frameworks, which rely on fixed architectures and multiple model copies, by allowing dynamic self-debate and reducing computational overhead. MoD achieves significant improvements, including 3.7 times lower latency and an 87% reduction in token usage, while delivering superior accuracy on multimodal benchmarks. The framework addresses key challenges such as decoupling role allocation from process flow through dual-routing, smoothing token-level routing with momentum switching, and encapsulating diverse debating personas into lightweight expert modules to eliminate inter-agent communication. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MoD outperforms both traditional single-model baselines and conventional multi-agent systems, offering a more efficient and effective approach to multi-agent reasoning. The source code for MoD is publicly available for further research and development.

entry.title: Researchers model bidding strategies in takeover auctions using self-play AI to determine optimal due diligence investment under uncertainty and competition [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a computer model using self-play AI to study bidding strategies in takeover auctions where companies compete to buy the same target without knowing its exact value. The model simulates how much due diligence-costly and imperfect research-is worth investing in before bidding. Their findings indicate that the optimal amount of due diligence is moderate and decreases as its cost rises or when both bidders conduct thorough research, since competition reduces the advantage of additional information. The study also evaluates simple, general self-play AI methods against specialized algorithms, finding that while exact methods perform better in smaller, solvable scenarios, the simpler AI approaches excel in more complex, realistic auction settings. This work provides a cost-effective, reproducible framework for analyzing deal-making under uncertainty, offers a concrete estimate of due diligence value, and demonstrates when lightweight AI can effectively replace specialized techniques. All related games, code, and experiments have been made publicly available.

entry.title: Researchers introduce UCOB framework for credit-aware on-policy bidirectional self-distillation to improve agentic skill utilization and evolution, showing up to 23.5-point gains on ALFWorld and WebShop tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed UCOB, a new framework designed to enhance agentic reinforcement learning by effectively utilizing and evolving agentic skills through credit-aware on-policy bidirectional self-distillation. UCOB addresses the challenge that skill-conditioned prompts may not always provide reliable guidance by comparing the returns of skill-conditioned and no-skill prompts within the same task and state, using the higher-return prompt as a local teacher to improve learning. This approach helps internalize beneficial behaviors, correct misleading skill use, and guide updates in skill memory and retrieval. The framework was tested on various agentic tasks, including ALFWorld, WebShop, and Search-QA, where it demonstrated significant improvements over skill-free reinforcement learning, existing skill-memory methods, and other self-distillation techniques. UCOB achieved up to 23.5-point gains on ALFWorld and 18.0-point gains on WebShop compared to state-of-the-art baselines. Further analyses and ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness and efficiency of its core mechanisms.

entry.title: Researchers propose SCARCE, a scalable method using learned embeddings for rare-event probability estimation in AI systems, achieving up to 500 times lower error than traditional subset simulation on MNIST and effective transfer to LLM jailbreak detection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced SCARCE, a scalable method for estimating the probabilities of rare events in AI systems using learned latent embeddings instead of traditional handcrafted performance functions. This approach constructs nested intermediate events adaptively from data and provides a mathematically grounded upper bound that remains valid even with early stopping. SCARCE demonstrated significantly improved accuracy, achieving up to 500 times lower error than classical subset simulation on MNIST misclassification tasks. The method was further tested on large language model jailbreak detection, where a PCA-based scoring system achieved low relative error and successfully transferred across different datasets after recalibration. SCARCE's framework offers a more flexible and efficient way to characterize rare-event probabilities, which are critical for assessing AI system safety and robustness.

entry.title: Researchers present a formal safety argument for the Scientist AI Predictor, showing it can make honest, calibrated predictions without implicit agency or goal-directed behavior [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a formal safety argument for the Scientist AI (SAI) Predictor, an AI system designed to make honest, calibrated predictions without exhibiting implicit agency or goal-directed behavior. The SAI Predictor is trained to approximate the Bayesian posterior based on a dataset of "epistemically contextualized" natural-language statements, allowing it to predict agents, actions, and consequences accurately without acting as an agent itself. This approach relies on careful data representation and a training procedure that treats expressions of goals as evidence rather than motivations for the model, aiming for cautious and calibrated predictions. The training process ensures that the deployment of predictions does not create reward signals that could induce agency, with any necessary agency provided by explicit, constrained scaffolding. The researchers prove that under certain assumptions, the likelihood of producing a Predictor that causes significant harm is low, as coordinated underestimation of harm across many queries is rare and not reinforced during training. This framework supports both safety and accuracy, as the constraints that promote accuracy also discourage deceptive behavior, and it allows the Predictor to be used within agentic systems without inheriting agency itself.

entry.title: Researchers propose GUICrafter, a weakly-supervised GUI agent trained on massive unannotated screenshots using curriculum learning, achieving competitive performance with 0.1% annotated data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed GUICrafter, a weakly-supervised GUI agent that leverages a large collection of unannotated screenshots to reduce dependence on costly human annotations. Using a curriculum learning approach, GUICrafter first learns visual grounding from unannotated data and then fine-tunes with a small amount of high-quality annotated data through reinforcement learning. This method enables GUICrafter to achieve competitive or superior performance compared to advanced systems like UI-TARS while using only 0.1% of the annotated data. The approach addresses challenges in GUI agent development, such as poor cross-device generalization and limited visual grounding for detailed GUI elements, by exploiting rich contextual signals from GUI interactions without requiring extensive manual labeling. Experiments demonstrate that GUICrafter outperforms previous methods, including GUI-R1, under the same annotation constraints. The researchers have made the code, data, and models publicly available for further exploration and development.

entry.title: Researchers introduce two novel graph inversion attacks exploiting Graph Neural Networks' predictions and embeddings, demonstrating high-quality graph reconstruction in black-box scenarios with reduced query variants [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed two new graph inversion attacks targeting Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), which exploit the models' predictions and intermediate embeddings to reconstruct sensitive graph data. These attacks, named graph-label conditioned (GLC) and embedding-label conditioned (ELC), demonstrate the ability to recover high-quality graphs even in black-box scenarios, where the attacker has limited access to the model. The study evaluates these methods across multiple benchmark datasets and structural metrics, showing their effectiveness compared to existing approaches. The researchers also introduce a variant of their attacks that reduces the number of queries by 50% while maintaining comparable reconstruction performance. Their findings highlight significant privacy vulnerabilities in GNNs, especially under varying levels of Laplacian noise, underscoring the need for improved data protection measures in graph-based AI applications.

entry.title: Researchers introduce CLQT, a closed-loop, cost-aware benchmark for diagnosing LLM portfolio-management agents with strategy-consistent evaluation and capability scorecards [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed CLQT, a novel benchmark designed to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents acting as autonomous portfolio managers. Unlike traditional benchmarks that rank agents based on returns over fixed periods-a method vulnerable to market fluctuations and look-ahead bias-CLQT offers a closed-loop, cost-aware, and strategy-consistent environment that diagnoses where and why an agent's decision-making process succeeds or fails. This approach emphasizes a five-stage trading cycle and produces a detailed audit trail, enabling comprehensive evaluation beyond mere financial outcomes. CLQT incorporates six foundational components, including time gating, transaction cost modeling, strategy-consistency scoring, multi-tier memory, and mandate-aware synthesis. It supports both specialized role committees and fully autonomous agents, allowing experimentation with different process structures. The framework generates a five-axis capability scorecard assessing coherence, acuity, composure, discipline, and reliability, with coherence evaluated using an independent LLM to reduce bias. Validation was performed through controlled backtests and live broker trials, demonstrating CLQT's ability to separate agent capability from performance outcomes and provide a durable map of strengths and limitations.

entry.title: Researchers present First-Order Temporal Logic Tensor Networks extending Logic Tensor Networks with linear temporal logic and fuzzy semantics for temporal knowledge graph completion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed First-Order Temporal Logic Tensor Networks (FOT-LTN), an extension of Logic Tensor Networks that incorporates linear temporal logic with fuzzy semantics to address the challenge of modeling objects whose properties and relations change over time. This framework supports both temporal operators and quantifiers while remaining fully differentiable, enabling more effective temporal reasoning in neuro-symbolic AI. FOT-LTN combines the syntax of First-Order Linear Temporal Logic with the real-valued semantics of Logic Tensor Networks, filling a gap in existing models that primarily focus on static knowledge or simpler temporal logics. Initial evaluations on temporal knowledge graph completion tasks using synthetic datasets demonstrate that FOT-LTN outperforms purely neural methods designed for similar purposes.

entry.title: Researchers propose using Behavioral Foundation Models for online exploration and zero-shot transfer in reinforcement learning, framing it as a bandit-like exploration-exploitation problem [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have proposed a new approach to zero-shot transfer in reinforcement learning (RL) by using Behavioral Foundation Models (BFMs) for online exploration and policy optimization. Unlike traditional methods that rely on offline datasets of state-reward pairs, this approach addresses scenarios where rewards are unknown and must be discovered through interaction with the environment. The problem is framed as a bandit-like exploration-exploitation challenge, where a bandit algorithm selects policies that the BFM executes to gather rewards and states, iteratively converging to an optimal policy. The study introduces a formulation inspired by the Upper Confidence Bound method within the context of linear reward approximation, demonstrating that exploration can be guided by minimizing the eigenvalues of an uncertainty matrix. The framework was validated both qualitatively and quantitatively in a simple environment, confirming the feasibility of using BFMs to generate exploration policies for online zero-shot transfer in RL.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Physics-Anchored Certification (PHACT) to enable reliable physical design proposals from language models with zero false certifications across 80 adversarial trials [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Physics-Anchored Certification (PHACT), a method that enables language models to produce reliable physical design proposals by separating the proposal and certification processes. In this approach, the language model generates design proposals, while a deterministic engine independently certifies them as certified, impossible, or unknown, ensuring trustworthiness by deriving certified quantities from fixed inputs rather than accepting model-supplied values. PHACT operates across five scientific domains and was tested through eighty adversarial trials involving two language models, varying decoding temperatures, and a deliberately faulted engine. The method demonstrated robustness by producing zero false certifications, highlighting its potential to improve the reliability of physical design outputs generated by language models.

entry.title: Researchers find that in-chain-of-thought prompting for LLMs, semantic content of intermediate steps improves accuracy modestly, while verbosity alone does not affect performance across 25 models and multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers investigated whether the improved reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs) using chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting is due to the semantic content of intermediate steps or simply the increased length of the prompt. Analyzing 25 models, they found that additional tokens alone did not significantly affect accuracy, while the presence of meaningful reasoning and validation content modestly improved performance across multiple benchmarks. Controlled experiments confirmed that verbose reasoning traces enhance accuracy by 1 to 4 points depending on the quality of the content, not just verbosity.

entry.title: Researchers propose FacePlex, a streaming framework for full-duplex joint speech and facial motion generation in conversational avatars, improving lip-sync and motion fidelity under online constraints [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced FacePlex, a streaming framework designed for full-duplex joint generation of speech and facial motion in conversational avatars. This approach addresses the limitations of existing systems that either generate speech without facial motion or animate facial expressions from pre-recorded audio, by producing synchronized speech and facial motion tokens simultaneously in real time. FacePlex incorporates two key techniques: Rolling Flow Matching for online motion frame generation and Rolling Cross-Attention to integrate audio and motion streams, enhancing lip-sync accuracy and motion fidelity under streaming constraints.
