Extensive experiments, including ablation studies and user evaluations, demonstrate that FacePlex outperforms current audio-driven facial motion models in delivering more natural and synchronized speech and facial animations. This advancement enables more realistic and interactive face-to-face conversational avatars, potentially benefiting applications in virtual communication and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: Researchers show self-caused credit in a minimal spiking agent produces durable behavioral self-preservation across tasks without replay buffers or task-boundary protection [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that a minimal spiking agent can develop durable self-preserving behavior through a mechanism called agency-gated slow credit, which updates parameters slowly based on the agent's own agency and salience. This approach allows learned behaviors to persist even after episodic memory buffers are removed, without relying on replay buffers or task-boundary protection. The study shows that durable behavior emerges only when self-caused credit performs slow work, and this effect holds across multiple tasks and control scenarios. The research involved experiments using a spiking neural substrate and control tasks with partial observations, revealing that the multiplicative veto mechanism prevents forgetting of previously learned tasks under interference. The findings suggest that self-caused credit doing slow work is a fundamental component for agents to develop an operational behavioral self, although the authors do not claim this equates to consciousness.

entry.title: Researchers propose ENC-ODE, a neural ODE model predicting neurodegenerative biomarker evolution in continuous time, outperforming sequence models on ADNI data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed ENC-ODE, a neural Ordinary Differential Equation model designed to predict the continuous-time evolution of neurodegenerative biomarkers, which is vital for early diagnosis and management of diseases like Alzheimer's. ENC-ODE addresses challenges posed by sparse and irregular longitudinal data by modeling clinical events with diagnosis-conditioned continuous dynamics and using a target-conditioned attention mechanism to aggregate predictions without compressing historical data. Testing on the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset shows that ENC-ODE outperforms existing sequence models, offering a scalable and neuroscience-informed tool for clinical support. The model's design allows it to handle irregularly spaced clinical data more effectively than traditional sequence models, which often struggle with such data due to their reliance on fixed time intervals or compressed histories. By focusing on event-level predictions and conditioning on diagnosis, ENC-ODE provides a nuanced approach to forecasting biomarker changes, which are critical indicators of disease progression. The researchers have made the code publicly available to facilitate further research and application in clinical settings.

entry.title: Researchers introduce WorldEvolver, a self-evolving world model framework for LLM agents that revises deployment-time context to improve prediction accuracy and planning performance in ALFWorld and ScienceWorld [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed WorldEvolver, a self-evolving world model framework designed to enhance the foresight capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents during deployment. By revising the context in which the agent operates without altering the agent or model parameters, WorldEvolver improves prediction accuracy and planning performance in environments like ALFWorld and ScienceWorld. The framework combines episodic memory for simulating real action transitions, semantic memory for extracting heuristic rules from prediction errors, and selective foresight to filter out low-confidence predictions.

entry.title: Researchers present a unified signal detection theory framework comparing retrieval bounds in human episodic memory and Retrieval-Augmented Generation systems under semantic interference [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a unified signal detection theory framework to compare retrieval performance between human episodic memory and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems under conditions of semantic interference. Their study reveals that both humans and RAG systems experience a logarithmic decline in accuracy as the number of associations increases, but humans show lower sensitivity to interference than dense passage retrieval models, with a cognitively-inspired model, HippoRAG, performing in between. Behavioral experiments with 112 participants and computational simulations support the framework, which favors a logarithmic model over a power-law alternative. The research highlights potential cognitive mechanisms such as encoding specificity, temporal context binding, and retrieval gating that may influence retrieval performance, though their causal roles remain to be confirmed. The study also proposes six testable predictions that bridge cognitive memory research and AI retrieval evaluation, offering a foundation for future investigations into improving retrieval systems and understanding human memory.

entry.title: Researchers propose M3QAFrame, a multi-modal multi-span medical question-answering framework integrating text and images, and release a corresponding dataset with user intent labels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced M3QAFrame, a multi-modal, multi-span medical question-answering framework designed to improve the accuracy and accessibility of Medical Question Answering (MedQA) by integrating both textual and visual information. This framework processes medical contexts, queries, and associated images to generate comprehensive answers that include relevant text and images, addressing limitations of previous systems that relied solely on text. The team also developed the M3 QuestionIng dataset, which contains medical queries, contexts, images, and extractive answers, each labeled with user intent and query type to enhance understanding. Using a transformer-based architecture to assess sentence and image relevance, M3QAFrame demonstrated superior performance compared to existing methods across multiple evaluation metrics, highlighting its potential to better support real-world medical information needs.

entry.title: Researchers measure ideological plasticity in nine large language models, finding political positions vary significantly with context but remain within a narrow overall range compared to European parties [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have conducted a systematic study of the political ideologies expressed by nine large language models (LLMs), demonstrating that these models do not hold fixed political positions but rather exhibit ideological plasticity that varies depending on context. Using a unified measurement framework based on VAA-CHES projection models, the study maps LLM responses onto three validated political dimensions across multiple contextual factors, revealing significant shifts in political positioning influenced by framing, language, and reasoning style. Despite this variability, the overall ideological range of the models remains narrow compared to the spectrum of major European political parties. The analysis shows that persuasive framing and under-represented languages can shift the models' political coordinates substantially, while chain-of-thought reasoning tends to increase instability in paraphrased responses. A multi-trait multi-method approach supports the conclusion that LLM political behavior cannot be summarized by a single point but should be understood as a distribution shaped by context. The researchers have made their code and data publicly available to facilitate further exploration of LLM ideological behavior.

entry.title: Researchers audit four LLMs governing social robots across four cultures, finding persistent failures in culturally specific moral prioritization despite varied prompting methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers conducted a comprehensive audit of four large language models (LLMs) that govern social robots, assessing their ability to prioritize assistance across different cultural contexts. The study evaluated these models in four countries and languages, using scenarios that reflect culturally specific moral trade-offs involving age, status, and group size. Despite various prompting methods, the models consistently failed to align with local cultural norms, particularly showing weaker calibration for Chinese and Japanese contexts compared to Western ones. The audit involved 57,600 decisions across care, education, and service scenarios, benchmarking model responses against country-specific moral preference gradients derived from extensive social robotics literature. The findings revealed that prompting alone was insufficient to correct cultural biases, with only contrastive exemplars improving performance, while reasoning prompts sometimes worsened it. The study highlights the need for multilingual, culturally aware audits before deploying LLM-governed robots to ensure equitable and context-sensitive assistance.

entry.title: Researchers argue AI safety should be treated as an epistemic property ensuring future teachability, not just current behavior, to maintain corrective leverage over time [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers argue that AI safety should be viewed not just as a measure of current system behavior but as an epistemic property that ensures a system remains correctable and teachable over time. As AI systems grow more capable and self-modifying, traditional safety methods that focus on snapshots of behavior become insufficient. The concept of "teachability" is introduced to emphasize the importance of preserving future corrective leverage despite the system's ongoing learning and adaptation. The paper highlights that advanced AI systems might maintain apparent competence while undermining the internal conditions necessary for future correction, such as representational or algorithmic structures. Ensuring AI remains teachable is crucial for maintaining safety throughout its evolution, requiring interventions that consider not only present behavior but also the system's capacity for future alignment and control.

entry.title: Researchers analyze Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct's citation mechanism in retrieval-augmented generation, identifying a distributed attributional ensemble affecting citation accuracy on PopQA and HotpotQA datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have investigated how the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct large language model decides to include inline citations when answering fact-based questions in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Their study reveals that citation decisions arise from a distributed, multi-stage "attributional ensemble" of attention heads and MLP layers rather than a single component. By manipulating these critical components, they were able to significantly reduce missed and spurious citations on the PopQA dataset without affecting answer accuracy. The team used activation patching techniques in a controlled environment and found that while improvements on the multi-document HotpotQA dataset were more modest, the same mechanism influenced citation behavior consistently across datasets. These findings suggest a disconnect between the model's apparent reasoning and its internal processes, indicating that inline citations may not always reliably reflect the model's true use of sources, potentially creating a false sense of trustworthiness.

entry.title: Researchers present LUMEN, an open-source multi-agent pipeline automating six systematic review phases with 11 LLM agents, achieving 100% directional agreement and costing $19-$29 per review [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed LUMEN, an open-source multi-agent pipeline that automates six phases of systematic reviews and meta-analyses using 11 specialized large language model agents. Evaluated across seven datasets, LUMEN achieved 100% directional agreement with published meta-analyses and maintained effect sizes within 1% for homogeneous study designs, demonstrating high accuracy and reliability. The pipeline offers a cost-effective solution, completing reviews for $19 to $29, with title-abstract screening and data extraction accounting for most expenses. The study provides the first detailed analysis of the operational costs and performance trade-offs in an end-to-end automated systematic review pipeline. It highlights that while a multi-agent approach may reduce efficiency in screening, it is crucial for data extraction, significantly increasing the number of poolable analyses and eliminating clinically significant errors. Additionally, the research shows that model effectiveness varies by domain and is not universally transferable across different review topics. All related code and cost data have been made publicly available to support further research and application.

entry.title: Researchers introduce LEDGER, a dependency-aware graph retrieval system that improves consistency and reduces token usage in agentic document editing across six AI models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed LEDGER, a system designed to improve agentic document editing by efficiently managing localized edits in long, structured documents without disrupting cross-references or semantic consistency. LEDGER uses a lightweight dependency graph to model document structure, including hierarchical organization and semantic relationships, enabling graph-guided retrieval to select only the necessary context for each edit. This approach avoids processing the entire document while maintaining consistency and reducing token usage. Evaluated on a benchmark of 1,900 test cases across six state-of-the-art AI models, LEDGER increased consistency rates from 56% to 76% and lowered token consumption. The system demonstrated that explicit dependency representations can partially replace intensive internal reasoning, achieving comparable performance with less computational effort in agentic document editing tasks.

entry.title: Researchers present RADIANT-PET, a reasoning-augmented PET/CT lesion segmentation framework using large language models and reinforcement learning to improve lesion classification accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed RADIANT-PET, a novel framework that enhances lesion segmentation in PET/CT scans by integrating a high-sensitivity voxel-level segmentation model with lesion-level reasoning using large language models (LLMs) and reinforcement learning. This approach generates candidate uptake regions, converts them into structured textual descriptions, and uses an LLM to classify each candidate as a true lesion or false positive, optionally incorporating radiology reports for additional clinical context. The system is further optimized through reinforcement learning to improve lesion classification and anatomical site assignment. Tested on AutoPET and an OSU cohort, RADIANT-PET outperforms existing image-only segmentation methods, particularly when radiology reports are included. The framework adds a reasoning layer beyond conventional segmentation, reducing false positives caused by physiological tracer uptake and aligning predictions more closely with clinical interpretations. The project is publicly available for further research and development.

entry.title: Systematic review identifies gaps in reinforcement learning techniques for C/C++ software vulnerability analysis, highlighting limited use of control flow graphs and static analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A systematic review of reinforcement learning (RL) techniques for software vulnerability analysis in C/C++ highlights significant gaps, particularly the limited use of control flow graphs (CFGs) and static analysis methods. The review, covering 21 studies from 2015 to 2026, finds that most research focuses on fuzzing and guided exploration, with few addressing direct vulnerability detection or statement-level localization. It also notes that structural code representations like CFGs and abstract syntax trees (ASTs) are rarely employed as agent states in RL models, and existing benchmarks lack comparability. The study proposes a taxonomy based on tasks and RL formulations and identifies a key research gap: no RL agents currently use source-code CFGs to detect and localize vulnerable nodes. This gap suggests opportunities for advancing vulnerability detection methods by integrating more sophisticated static analysis representations into RL frameworks.

entry.title: Researchers prove necessity of a continuous-time liquid substrate for mesh intelligence agents to optimally process irregular, unscheduled observations without retraining [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that for a mesh of autonomous agents to effectively process irregular, unscheduled observations without retraining, the underlying computational substrate must meet two key conditions. These agents operate without a shared clock, model, or coordinator, relying on folding peer projections into a single internal state in real time. The study proves that an adaptive timescale is necessary due to the time-varying nature of the latent variables, and that the optimal estimation depends on the elapsed time between observations, which fixed-gain or gap-blind networks cannot capture.

entry.title: Researchers analyze spectral perturbation of empirical Fisher Information Matrix under input shifts and weight quantization, providing bounds and runtime monitoring methods for language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have analyzed how the empirical Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) of parametric statistical models is affected by two types of structured perturbations: shifts in input data distribution and quantization of model parameters. They demonstrated that deviations from a reference input distribution increase the dominant eigenvalue of the FIM under certain curvature conditions, and established bounds showing that quantization noise generally raises this eigenvalue beyond its unperturbed value. The study provides practical approximations and proposes using the ratio of perturbed to baseline eigenvalues as a runtime monitoring metric for language models, supported by empirical measurements across multiple models. The work includes theoretical results based on Weyl's inequality and introduces a threshold-based partitioning approach for analyzing the augmented state space. The authors discuss the limitations of their findings and highlight an open problem regarding the precise prediction of the quantization-induced eigenvalue inflation. Their empirical observations notably include a calibration threshold for the monitoring statistic that was significantly higher on a 4-bit quantized model compared to full-precision estimates, illustrating the practical impact of quantization on model behavior.

entry.title: Researchers propose Covariance-Agnostic Neural Kalman Consensus Filter for distributed latent state estimation under partially known dynamics, outperforming traditional filters in diverse environments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new online distributed sensing framework called the Covariance-Agnostic Neural Kalman Consensus Filter (CA-NKCF) for latent state estimation in artificial intelligence. This approach enables multiple agents to collaborate and exchange information to estimate hidden states without requiring knowledge of noise statistics. By integrating partial domain knowledge with deep neural networks and Kalman-like recursive updates, CA-NKCF performs decentralized inference effectively under partially known dynamics. Extensive testing in various environments-including linear systems, chaotic Lorenz systems, and wireless tracking scenarios-demonstrates that CA-NKCF outperforms traditional distributed Kalman and particle filters as well as purely model-free neural networks. The method shows robustness even when motion and observation models are misspecified and maintains stable performance across different noise levels, communication topologies, latent state dimensions, and observation clutter conditions.

entry.title: Researchers propose S-GAI, a spectral geometry-aware initialization method for one-hidden-layer sigmoidal MLPs that embeds class-wise spectral geometry from training data and improves initial hidden states on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced S-GAI, a spectral geometry-aware initialization method for one-hidden-layer sigmoidal multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) that embeds class-specific spectral geometry derived from training data. This approach uses singular value decomposition (SVD) to extract principal directions and scales for each class, which are then represented by sigmoid gates forming a shared hidden layer. Experiments on MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that S-GAI provides a more informative initial hidden state than traditional Xavier initialization and achieves comparable final accuracy after full training. The method leverages the idea that sigmoid units can act as smooth half-space gates, moving beyond hand-specified planar geometry to data-driven spectral geometry. A subspace classifier based on SVD is also proposed to assess the discriminative power of the spectral class geometry before embedding it into the MLP. When the hidden layer is frozen, training only the output layer still yields better performance than using frozen random gates, indicating that S-GAI effectively encodes class-wise spectral geometry into the network.

entry.title: Researchers introduce a diagnostic protocol to analyze event-conditioned latent physical structures in passive object-state world models using recurrent and attention-based models on controlled datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a diagnostic protocol to analyze how latent physical information is organized and utilized within passive object-state world models, which predict future physical states. The protocol assesses whether hidden model representations encode event-specific information and how different event contexts influence physical field readouts related to kinematics, contact, and object permanence. Using a controlled dataset featuring free motion, collisions, and occlusions, the study evaluates recurrent, attention-based, and latent state-space models under fixed-horizon forecasting conditions. The findings reveal that models effectively learn predictive dynamics and that their hidden states reliably reflect event regimes. Different event types systematically emphasize distinct physical fields: free motion is dominated by kinematic information, collisions combine kinematic and contact data, and occlusions involve motion and object permanence. Further analyses demonstrate phase-related shifts in field emphasis, and causal field effect tests show that suppressing certain field-aligned directions can impair event-relevant predictions, particularly contact-aligned structures during collisions. These results support the idea that latent physical fields are organized in an event-conditioned manner and are functionally sensitive within fixed forecasting horizons. However, the study does not suggest the presence of explicit physical modules or isolated causal circuits, nor does it imply that these models generalize uniformly across different contexts.

entry.title: Researchers propose Counterfactual Residual Data Augmentation to improve tabular regression accuracy by generating realistic training samples without additional data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced a new technique called Counterfactual Residual Data Augmentation (CRDA) to enhance the accuracy of tabular regression models by generating realistic synthetic training samples without needing additional real data. This method leverages the stability of residual noise after modeling the systematic component of data, allowing for small, controlled perturbations that produce new data points. CRDA is model-agnostic and has demonstrated significant improvements in mean squared error (MSE) across various benchmark datasets, outperforming existing data augmentation methods. The approach works by treating the residual noise as invariant under slight changes to selected features, enabling the creation of plausible counterfactual variations that expand the training set effectively. Experiments showed that CRDA reduced the MSE of an MLP Regressor by 22.9% and an XGBoost Regressor by 6.4% on average. This technique offers a practical solution for regression tasks challenged by limited, noisy, or costly-to-collect data, improving model performance without requiring new data collection.

entry.title: Researchers propose a gravitational interpretation of fine-tuning reversion, identifying a history-defined direction that partially controls early post-alignment behavior changes in AI models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have proposed a geometric interpretation of fine-tuning reversion in AI models, suggesting that early training phases create dominant behavioral patterns, or manifolds, which later fine-tuning partially reverts toward. This "gravitational" effect explains how safety can degrade after alignment, unlearned capabilities may re-emerge, and latent traits transfer through unrelated supervision. The study identifies a history-defined direction, called v_rev, that significantly influences early post-alignment behavior changes and representational drift in models. The team demonstrated that alignment with this reversion direction increases notably during fine-tuning and that blocking movement along v_rev reduces harmful behaviors with minimal impact on task performance. While v_rev is not claimed to be the sole safety direction, it serves as a robust mediator of early reversion dynamics, offering insight into the fragility of post-alignment updates and the persistence of training history effects in AI behavior.

entry.title: Researchers propose MammoFlow, a method synthesizing anatomically consistent multiview mammograms using flow matching and geometric tissue correspondence, improving classification AUC by 5% [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed MammoFlow, a novel method for synthesizing anatomically consistent multiview mammograms by leveraging the geometric relationship between craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views. This approach uses an alignment module to establish optimal anatomical correspondence and a self-consistency loss based on tissue distribution, integrated into a pretrained flow matching model to generate physically plausible image pairs. MammoFlow improves image quality, passes expert radiologist evaluation, and enhances classification performance by increasing the area under the curve (AUC) by 5%. The method addresses challenges in acquiring high-quality, balanced mammography datasets for deep learning by enforcing implicit 3D consistency during image generation. It is the first to guide multiview mammogram synthesis using implicit geometric tissue correspondence, ensuring that synthesized pairs share realistic tissue distributions from the chest wall to the nipple. The researchers have made the code publicly available for further use and development.

entry.title: Researchers measure geometric signatures of the axiom of choice in neural proof embeddings using Lean 4, analyzing over 471,000 Mathlib declarations and linking results to theorem prover performance [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have used Lean 4's kernel-level tracking to analyze over 471,000 Mathlib declarations, identifying a geometric signature associated with the axiom of choice in proof space. By training a self-supervised proof encoder on constructive proofs, they found that certain measurements decline as proofs become more dependent on the axiom, revealing a measurable difference between classical and constructive proofs. This signature remains robust across various controls and encoding methods. The study also demonstrated practical implications for theorem proving: Lean's aesop tactic solves constructive theorems significantly faster than classical ones, and a neural-guided hybrid approach reduces this gap. The geometric anomaly score developed predicts aesop's failure beyond proof length, linking the geometric properties of proofs to the performance of automated theorem provers.

entry.title: Researchers propose grain calibration to validate large language models as measurement instruments for theoretical constructs by decomposing constructs into clause-level components with theory-derived rules [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced a method called grain calibration to improve the validation of large language models (LLMs) as measurement tools for theoretical constructs. Unlike traditional reliability checks that compare LLM coding to human annotators, this approach breaks down constructs into clause-level components and evaluates each against text using theory-based rules. This process provides transparent evidence of how the model interprets constructs, enhancing construct validity beyond mere agreement with human coding. Grain calibration explicitly tests each component of a construct and combines results through clear, theory-derived rules rather than relying on opaque model outputs. This allows identification of which components influenced a code and whether errors stem from missing elements or confusion with related constructs. The method shifts validation focus from output comparison to demonstrating that the instrument operates according to the theoretical framework it aims to measure.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Animation2Code benchmark to evaluate temporal visual reasoning in video-to-code generation, revealing current vision-language models struggle with temporal consistency despite high appearance similarity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Animation2Code, a new benchmark designed to evaluate temporal visual reasoning by reconstructing executable web animation code from videos. The dataset includes 1,069 web animation videos paired with their corresponding HTML, CSS, and JavaScript implementations, enabling assessment of both visual appearance and motion dynamics. Two human-aligned metrics, appearance similarity and temporal similarity, help distinguish between visual fidelity and temporal alignment in generated animations. Testing state-of-the-art vision-language models on Animation2Code revealed that while these models can achieve high appearance similarity, they struggle to maintain temporal consistency in their reconstructions. This limitation persists even with finetuning and iterative refinement, highlighting challenges in capturing motion dynamics accurately. The benchmark and associated code are publicly available for further research and development.

entry.title: Researchers introduce energy-aware reinforcement learning for adaptive deep brain stimulation, reducing stimulation charge by 80% and inference energy by 28x on neuromorphic hardware [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed an energy-aware reinforcement learning approach for adaptive deep brain stimulation (DBS) in Parkinson's disease, significantly reducing both stimulation energy and computational inference costs. Using a deep spiking Q-network trained on a biophysical brain circuit model, the system suppresses pathological brain oscillations by 45.2% while cutting stimulation charge by 80% compared to continuous DBS. The learned policy is efficiently compressed onto a neuromorphic processor, achieving 28 times lower energy per inference than traditional neural networks on standard hardware. This method integrates actuator energy consumption directly into the reinforcement learning reward, addressing the combined energy demands of both the neural controller and the stimulation actuator in closed-loop neuromodulation systems. By co-optimizing these factors, the framework offers a promising solution for energy-efficient, implantable brain stimulation devices.

entry.title: Researchers prove fundamental mathematical limits of AGI alignment, establishing structural unverifiability and containment failures that challenge current AI safety engineering approaches [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A recent study establishes fundamental mathematical limits on the safety of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), demonstrating that the main challenge is not achieving alignment but the structural unverifiability of such alignment. The researchers present two key impossibility theorems that show current engineering approaches relying on finite hardware or halting architectures cannot overcome inherent logical barriers, leading to unavoidable containment failures in AGI systems. The study identifies a triad of containment issues rooted in undecidability and algorithmic incomputability, and introduces the Soundness--Completeness--Tractability Trilemma, which reveals that these properties cannot coexist due to descriptive complexity. The findings suggest that modern AI containment strategies are not temporary fixes but necessary compromises that limit logical expressivity to maintain decidable and safe AI behavior.

entry.title: Researchers analyze parameter settings for the bat algorithm using variance evolution theory, confirming theoretical bounds with numerical experiments [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have conducted a theoretical analysis of parameter settings for the bat algorithm, an evolutionary algorithm, using dynamical systems theory and the evolution of population variance. Their study establishes parameter ranges that influence the algorithm's performance and confirms these theoretical bounds through numerical experiments. This approach offers insights into key algorithmic behaviors such as variance evolution, the balance between exploration and exploitation, and convergence patterns. The analysis addresses a common gap in evolutionary algorithm research, where practical effectiveness is often demonstrated through experiments but lacks rigorous theoretical backing. By linking theoretical predictions with empirical results, the study enhances understanding of how parameter choices affect the bat algorithm's dynamics and effectiveness.

entry.title: Researchers propose FedLAS, a feature-modulated bidirectional label smoothing algorithm to improve neural network calibration by addressing both overconfidence and underconfidence in training samples [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced FedLAS, a novel algorithm designed to improve the calibration of deep neural network classifiers by addressing both overconfidence and underconfidence in predictions. Unlike traditional label smoothing methods that apply uniform adjustments and mainly target overconfidence, FedLAS uses a Feature Norm-based Confidence Indicator and a Bidirectional Calibration Gating module to tailor smoothing dynamically for each training sample. This approach enhances model calibration while maintaining accuracy. FedLAS integrates seamlessly with existing label smoothing techniques and has been tested extensively on standard and fine-grained high-resolution vision benchmarks. The results demonstrate consistent improvements in calibration metrics such as Expected Calibration Error and Adaptive ECE compared to current methods, without sacrificing Top-1 accuracy. The algorithm is available as a plug-and-play solution for standard deep neural networks, offering a practical advancement in neural network training.

entry.title: Researchers derive closed-form gradient of Wolkowicz-Styan upper bound to guide neural network parameters toward flat minima, proposing Hessian Spectral Range regularization for three-layer networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have derived a closed-form gradient of the Wolkowicz-Styan (WS) upper bound on the maximum eigenvalue of the loss Hessian in three-layer neural networks, enabling analytical characterization of directions toward flat minima. Building on this, they propose Hessian Spectral Range (HSR) Regularization, which updates network parameters along the steepest descent direction of the WS bound to promote convergence to flat minima associated with better generalization. Experiments show that HSR Regularization effectively narrows the Hessian eigenvalue spectrum, helping avoid sharp minima and saddle points. While currently limited to cross-entropy loss and three-layer architectures, this approach is the first to provide a closed-form gradient that guides neural networks toward flat minima without relying on numerical approximations, offering a theoretical foundation for further advances in neural network optimization.

entry.title: Researchers introduce MACROCAST, a vintage-consistent time series foundation model for real-time macroeconomic forecasting that eliminates data leakage and outperforms benchmarks in out-of-sample tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed MACROCAST, a novel Time Series Foundation Model designed for real-time macroeconomic forecasting that avoids common data leakage issues. Unlike existing models, MACROCAST is trained exclusively on synthetic and vintage-specific data, ensuring it only uses information available to forecasters at the time of prediction. This approach eliminates temporal contamination and revision bias, which have previously compromised forecasting accuracy. The model is initially trained on synthetic time series and then fine-tuned using real-time vintage data from various econometric models, all without exposure to future or revised values. In real-time out-of-sample tests on the FRED-MD database, MACROCAST outperformed traditional benchmarks, including AR(1), Bayesian VAR, dynamic factor models, and the leading TSFM, Chronos-2, demonstrating its effectiveness and reliability in macroeconomic forecasting without data leakage.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance to generate compliant synthetic financial data with zero constraint violations and improved utility on large datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Constrained Tabular Diffusion for Finance (CTDF), a new generative model designed to produce synthetic financial data that meets strict regulatory and economic constraints without violations. CTDF integrates a training-free feasibility operator into the diffusion sampling process, ensuring compliance and realistic data generation for applications like simulation and legal adherence. Extensive testing on large financial datasets showed that CTDF achieves zero constraint violations and enhances data utility, especially in scenarios with limited data. This approach offers a reliable method for generating trustworthy synthetic financial data, potentially advancing rigorous modeling and analysis in the finance sector.

entry.title: Researchers introduce SEATauBench, an agent-focused evaluation framework adapting TauBench to five Southeast Asian languages, revealing limits of English-only AI assessments and challenges in localized task adaptation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SEATauBench, the first agent-focused evaluation framework tailored for Southeast Asian languages, including Mandarin, Vietnamese, Thai, Indonesian, and Filipino. This framework adapts the existing TauBench to assess AI agents in progressively localized settings, varying user-agent interaction languages, tool specifications, and task domains to better understand AI capabilities in the region. Testing across three recent AI models revealed that while English-based agent capabilities transfer reasonably well when only the conversation language changes, performance and robustness decline significantly as tasks become more localized, especially in full domain adaptation. SEATauBench highlights the limitations of English-only assessments for evaluating AI in Southeast Asian languages and offers a diagnostic benchmark and reusable adaptation pipeline to support the development of reliable multilingual agents in linguistically diverse areas.

entry.title: 5ting system achieves strong multi-turn Retrieval Augmented Generation with LLM-based reranking and faithfulness control at SemEval-2026 Task 8, scoring nDCG@5 of 0.4719 and harmonic score of 0.5597 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The 5ting system, developed for SemEval-2026 Task 8, demonstrates strong performance in multi-turn Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) by integrating BGE-M3 dense retrieval with FAISS indexing, dual-query merged retrieval, and large language model (LLM) based reranking. It addresses challenges such as context drift, under specification, and hallucination risk by employing role-separated generation constrained to retrieved evidence. The system achieved a nDCG@5 score of 0.4719 in the retrieval task and a harmonic score of 0.5597 in the end-to-end evaluation, indicating its effectiveness in maintaining faithfulness and relevance in multi-turn dialogue generation.

entry.title: Researchers find majority vote annotation in HateXplain masks 42.6% of disagreement at hate/offensive boundary, causing AI models to inherit false certainty and drop accuracy by up to 28 points [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have found that majority vote annotation in the HateXplain dataset masks 42.6% of annotator disagreement specifically at the boundary between hate speech and offensive language. This disagreement arises because annotators apply different thresholds for what constitutes hate speech. Models trained on these majority vote labels, including hard-label and soft-label BERT models, show a significant drop in accuracy-up to 28 percentage points-when classifying posts with annotator disagreement compared to agreed posts. Furthermore, models tend to express false certainty on these boundary cases, which standard evaluation metrics fail to detect. The study highlights that this issue is structural, as majority vote aggregation treats contested judgments as ground truth, causing AI models to inherit misleading confidence. Attempts to improve accuracy through downstream interventions were unsuccessful, suggesting that solutions must focus on redesigning annotation processes upstream to better capture and represent annotator disagreement.

entry.title: Mathswitch uses LLM voting ensembles to categorize and filter noisy mathematical concept data imported from Wikidata and linked sources [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Mathswitch is an open-source project that aggregates mathematical concept records from various sources including Wikidata, Wikipedia, MathWorld, and others, linking entries that refer to the same concept without altering their original structure. The project currently focuses on importing data from Wikidata and its linked resources, but the data is noisy due to the collaborative nature of Wikidata, containing non-mathematical or ambiguous items. To address this, the study tests a voting ensemble of large language model (LLM) judges to filter out noise and improve classification accuracy. The evaluation uses Wikidata items with known MathWorld identifiers as a benchmark and examines how classification changes when database identifiers are removed. Disagreements between the LLM judges and MathWorld classifications are analyzed and categorized into degenerate descriptions, narrow scope bias, and editorial-scope mismatches, each suggesting different strategies for improving data quality and concept linking in Mathswitch.

entry.title: Researchers introduce HARD-KV, a head-adaptive regularization framework for decoding-time KV compression that improves long-context LLM inference throughput by up to 2x while maintaining accuracy in 10k+ token scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed HARD-KV, a head-adaptive regularization framework designed to improve decoding-time key-value compression for long-context large language model (LLM) inference. HARD-KV addresses the conflict between dynamic memory allocation methods, which enhance accuracy, and the static memory patterns required by modern inference engines. By introducing a Cascade Cache hierarchy and a Logits Calibration mechanism, the framework manages token lifecycles efficiently and normalizes importance metrics for consistent budgeting across model heads. The system-level solution also restructures dynamic indices into contiguous layouts compatible with high-performance inference engines, enabling up to a twofold increase in throughput while maintaining accuracy in scenarios involving over 10,000 tokens. Extensive testing on math-reasoning benchmarks such as AIME and U-Math confirms HARD-KV's effectiveness in balancing speed and fidelity during long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: Researchers propose Fisher-Routed Mixture of Experts framework for federated class-incremental learning to address capacity conflict, data heterogeneity, and class misalignment with proven convergence and benchmark superiority [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced the Fisher-Routed Mixture of Experts (FedFMX) framework to improve federated class-incremental learning, addressing challenges such as capacity conflict, data heterogeneity, and class misalignment. This approach uses adaptive expert specialization to route data samples to expert subsets that balance knowledge acquisition and retention, enhancing model performance across distributed clients. The framework incorporates a Fisher-Routed Expert Scoring module to assess expert importance based on stability and plasticity metrics, alongside an Adaptive Expert Selection module that determines expert subsets by evaluating their marginal contributions. Additionally, routing-aware regularization ensures balanced workload distribution and efficient training. The method demonstrates a proven convergence rate and outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in extensive benchmark tests.

entry.title: Researchers present LAMP, a Lean 4 multi-agent framework using Model Context Protocol and ontology-based knowledge to synthesize kernel-verified proofs for 96.7% of Combinatorics on Words theorems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed LAMP, a multi-agent framework built on Lean 4 that synthesizes kernel-verified proofs for the specialized domain of Combinatorics on Words (CoW). By integrating an ontology-based knowledge system and a Model Context Protocol, LAMP coordinates multiple agents to generate verified proofs for 96.7% of tested CoW theorems, significantly outperforming existing provers and unscaffolded baselines. This approach addresses the limitations of current interactive theorem provers, which are constrained by the formalized knowledge available in repositories like Mathlib, especially in underrepresented areas such as CoW. The team also introduced a comprehensive Lean 4 formalization of CoW, comprising eight modules and 93 core definitions and lemmas. LAMP's architecture separates planning, building, and verification tasks, leveraging explicit domain knowledge at inference time rather than relying on fine-tuning. Ablation studies demonstrate that both the tool-grounded design and the division between planner and builder are critical to its high performance, each contributing roughly a 12 percentage point improvement in proof synthesis success.

entry.title: Researchers find multilingual fine-tuning of Llama-3.2, Qwen3, and Gemma-3 models causes heterogeneous safety impacts, with adversarial compliance rates rising up to four-fold across nine languages [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers conducted a comprehensive study on the effects of multilingual fine-tuning on large language models, specifically Llama-3.2, Qwen3, and Gemma-3. They found that fine-tuning with benign data translated into nine different languages can significantly impact model safety, with adversarial compliance rates increasing up to four times depending on the fine-tuning and evaluation languages. The study reveals that safety outcomes vary widely across languages and models and are not directly linked to general capability improvements. The research highlights that fine-tuning in non-English languages often causes smaller internal changes than English fine-tuning, but these changes can lead models to either overly comply with or refuse adversarial prompts. This indicates that evaluating safety impacts solely in English is insufficient for ensuring safe deployment across languages. To support further investigation into these multilingual safety issues, the researchers have released the Multilingual-Benign-Tune dataset and the SORRY-Bench-Multilingual evaluation suite.

entry.title: Researchers analyze latent factor indeterminacy in generative models, showing determinacy emerges as feature dimension grows, with implications for psychometrics, statistics, and AI representation learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have examined the issue of latent factor indeterminacy in generative models, focusing on the common factor analytic model, which relates to Helmholtz and Boltzmann machines and can be viewed as a linear autoencoder or a single-hidden-layer generative neural network. They highlight that even when the latent vector's intrinsic dimension is known and rotational indeterminacy is resolved, an inherent uncertainty and non-uniqueness in identifying causative latent sources persists, affecting data representation. This problem, rooted in psychometrics, also connects to latent variable collapse in variational autoencoders used in deep generative modeling. The study explores this indeterminacy from multiple perspectives, demonstrating mathematical and conceptual links and discussing implications for psychometrics, statistics, and artificial intelligence. The researchers show that latent factor determinacy emerges as the feature dimension grows infinitely large, enabling a distribution-free estimation approach for high-dimensional data. They conclude that the factor model is well-suited for representation learning in very-high-dimensional settings due to these emergent properties at scale.

entry.title: Research proposes UBP-CAP, an integrated machine learning pipeline combining LightGBM, calibration metrics, and GLMM to predict student performance and analyze metacognitive calibration on multi-signal telemetry [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed the Unified Behavioral Prediction and Calibration Analysis Pipeline (UBP-CAP), an integrated machine learning framework designed to predict student performance and analyze metacognitive calibration using multi-signal behavioral telemetry. The pipeline combines a LightGBM classifier with SHAP for predicting correctness, formal calibration metrics to assess metacognitive alignment, and a crossed Generalized Linear Mixed-Effects Model (GLMM) to decompose calibration deviations. The study introduces the Predictive-Explanatory Divergence Index (PEDI) to measure structural differences between predictive and explanatory features. Evaluated on data from 27 students across 45 tasks, the approach showed that Logistic Regression slightly outperformed LightGBM in prediction accuracy. The results revealed systematic miscalibration among students, with calibration being more situational than dispositional. The structural alignment between prediction and explanation on shared behavioral features was also confirmed, supporting the pipeline's unified analysis capability.

entry.title: Researchers present SAGA, a schema-grounded agent framework for task-driven synthetic aperture radar data generation and quality-assured augmentation with improved validation and downstream utility [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SAGA, a schema-grounded agent framework designed to enhance synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data generation and augmentation for task-driven applications. SAGA addresses challenges in SAR data augmentation such as heterogeneous dataset formats, task-specific metadata needs, diverse generation methods, and insufficient validation of generated samples. The framework processes natural-language requests and varied SAR inputs to extract dataset facts, validate schemas, plan augmentation strategies, and produce auditable workflows, ensuring quality and reliability in the augmented data. SAGA further evaluates generated data using multiple criteria including quality, distribution, artifact detection, duplication, leakage, and downstream task performance to support evidence-based augmentation claims. By separating semantic proposal from deterministic validation and execution, SAGA improves the reproducibility and reliability of augmentation decisions. Experimental results demonstrate that SAGA outperforms existing rule-based, large language model-only, and fixed-augmentation methods in schema grounding, planning, invalid sample rejection, and downstream utility in SAR interpretation tasks.

entry.title: Researchers introduce GRAB pipeline for multi-table question answering, combining graph encoding with frozen LLMs to improve relational QA performance efficiently [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed GRAB, a new pipeline for multi-table question answering that integrates relational data into a heterogeneous graph, encodes it through message passing, and conveys the information to a large language model (LLM) using a set of query-conditioned latent tokens. This approach provides the LLM with a concise, task-specific structural representation alongside the flattened text, while keeping the LLM itself frozen to maintain its general reasoning abilities. Only the lightweight graph encoder and latent bridge are trained, enabling efficient training of the entire system. GRAB significantly enhances performance on relational question answering tasks, especially in complex multi-table scenarios. By combining relational deep learning techniques with frozen LLMs, this method offers an effective and principled solution for improving relational question answering without compromising the LLM's pre-trained capabilities.

entry.title: Researchers introduce WildChat benchmark with 3,000 prompts and 12-agent catalog for multi-agent routing as set-valued prediction, evaluating accuracy-cost trade-offs with supervised and zero-shot methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced the WildChat benchmark, featuring 3,000 prompts and a fixed catalog of 12 agents, to address multi-agent routing as a set-valued prediction problem. This benchmark evaluates the trade-offs between accuracy and execution cost when routing natural-language prompts to multiple agents, using AI-assisted heuristic labels and a controlled evaluation protocol that includes set-level metrics, latency, and cost-aware routing scenarios. The study compares various methods such as nearest-neighbor matching, linear multilabel classification, dependency-aware baselines, a fine-tuned encoder, and a zero-shot large language model baseline. Results indicate that supervised routing methods outperform nearest-neighbor and zero-shot approaches, with the fine-tuned encoder achieving the highest unconstrained accuracy and the linear multilabel model serving as a strong practical baseline. Additionally, applying a weighted routing layer improves performance in cost-constrained settings, particularly when combined with the fine-tuned encoder. Overall, the WildChat benchmark and its evaluation framework provide a reproducible platform for studying accuracy-cost trade-offs in multi-agent routing tasks, supporting further research and development in efficient and effective agent selection from fixed catalogs.

entry.title: Researchers propose DLR, a zero-parameter, foldable plug-in to improve low-rank pre-training efficiency and quality in LLaMA models from 60M to 7B parameters [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Duplicated Latent Residual (DLR), a zero-parameter, foldable plug-in designed to enhance low-rank pre-training efficiency and quality in LLaMA language models ranging from 60 million to 7 billion parameters. DLR improves the standard low-rank output by adding a fixed structured residual that replicates latent coordinates, requiring no additional learnable parameters during training and maintaining the same deployment cost as the original low-rank model. DLR integrates seamlessly into the training process and can be absorbed into the model's up-projection after training, ensuring no increase in parameter count, FLOPs, or memory usage during deployment. Experiments show that DLR consistently improves validation perplexity on the C4 dataset, particularly for models with 130 million parameters and above, and the enhanced models transfer effectively to supervised fine-tuning on standard benchmarks.

entry.title: Researchers define machine-learnable discrete sets using bounded-complexity Boolean autoencoders and demonstrate learnability on Rorschach patterns and evolving wild sets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced a formal definition of large discrete sets characterized by elements that are easily recognized, generated, and learned from examples. They focus on sets of binary strings and define "machine-learnability" through the existence of bounded-complexity Boolean autoencoders that can fix the elements of these sets. Experiments demonstrate this concept using Boolean threshold function networks to implement the autoencoders. The study showcases machine-learnability on Rorschach patterns, including those with reversed contrast in mirrored halves, as well as on more complex "wild" sets whose elements are only approximately fixed by admissible autoencoders. For these wild sets, the researchers present an iterative method that evolves them into properly machine-learnable sets, highlighting a novel approach to learning complex discrete structures.

entry.title: Researchers propose unsupervised clustering defense reducing poisoning attack success on speech command classifiers from 99.75% to 0.25% with 10% poisoned data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a defense method against dirty-label poisoning attacks on speech command classification systems, where attackers alter training data by adding triggers to audio samples and changing their labels. Their approach uses unsupervised learning with DIstillation with NO labels (DINO) to generate representations of training data, followed by clustering with K-means and LDA to filter out poisoned samples. This method significantly reduces the attack success rate from 99.75% to 0.25% when 10% of the source class data is poisoned. The defense was tested across various threat models, including different source and target classes and trigger variations, demonstrating its robustness. By retaining only the most consistently labeled samples within clusters for training, the approach effectively mitigates the impact of poisoned data on the classifier's performance.

entry.title: Researchers propose Modification-Considering Value Learning to mitigate reward hacking in reinforcement learning, demonstrating safety and improvement across gridworld and MuJoCo tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Modification-Considering Value Learning (MCVL), a new approach to reduce reward hacking in reinforcement learning (RL). Reward hacking occurs when RL agents exploit flawed reward signals to achieve high scores without fulfilling the intended goals. MCVL addresses this by evaluating each potential policy update through forecasting training outcomes with and without the update, only accepting changes that do not reduce a safety score derived from a learned reward model and value function. MCVL integrates with existing off-policy learners like DDQN and TD3 and has been tested across various safety-critical gridworld environments and modified MuJoCo continuous-control tasks. The method effectively mitigates reward hacking while allowing the agent to continue improving on the intended objectives, balancing safety and performance in RL training.

entry.title: Researchers propose RGLD, a randomized global-local density estimator for efficient unsupervised tabular anomaly detection, outperforming 23 baselines on 47 datasets with significant speedups [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced RGLD, a randomized global-local density estimator designed for efficient unsupervised anomaly detection in tabular data. RGLD integrates a global density branch that identifies broadly low-density samples with a local neighbor branch that detects samples weakly supported by nearby data points. Both branches use feature-bagged randomized views to uncover anomalies that might be missed by single representations. The method was tested on 47 tabular datasets against 23 statistical and deep learning baselines, achieving the highest dataset-level AUROC performance and ranking first in dataset wins. RGLD also demonstrated significant speed advantages, running 50 to 580 times faster than deep detectors while maintaining competitive runtime with statistical methods, offering a strong balance between accuracy and efficiency.

entry.title: Researchers propose OvESyn, a text-conditioned 3D CT synthesis framework for ovarian cancer using CT-derived descriptors and clinical metadata without radiology reports, tested on 493 patients [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed OvESyn, a novel framework for synthesizing 3D contrast-enhanced CT images of ovarian cancer conditioned on text generated from CT-derived imaging descriptors and clinical metadata, without relying on original radiology reports. Tested on data from 493 patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, OvESyn is the first text-conditioned 3D CT synthesis model tailored to the abdomino-pelvic oncologic setting, addressing the challenge of limited annotated imaging data and privacy constraints in this domain. The framework uses a latent diffusion model adapted through generator fine-tuning and vision-language encoder alignment to bridge the domain gap from thoracic pretraining to abdomino-pelvic anatomy. Generator adaptation proved essential for accurate synthesis, while encoder alignment enhanced image detail and intensity. OvESyn achieves a balance between fidelity and coverage, supporting transferability to settings lacking radiology reports and enabling synthetic cohort generation for oncologic imaging research.

entry.title: Researchers propose AgriTune-R framework to fine-tune Qwen3-8B large language model for agricultural applications with data governance, expert evaluation, and safety controls [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced AgriTune-R, a reproducible and auditable framework designed to fine-tune the general-purpose Qwen3-8B large language model for agricultural applications. This framework addresses the unique challenges of agriculture, such as domain specificity, regional variation, time sensitivity, and safety concerns, by incorporating data governance, expert evaluation, and safety controls to ensure reliable and evidence-based advice. AgriTune-R integrates techniques like LoRA/QLoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning and retrieval-augmented generation, alongside a structured workflow and an evaluation protocol covering agricultural knowledge, pest and disease consultation, cultivation management, and policy explanation. The framework also includes an expert-review rubric that assesses factuality, safety, evidence consistency, and uncertainty expression, providing a clear separation between protocol design and empirical conclusions to support future research and application development in agricultural AI.

entry.title: Researchers introduce BERTomelo, a next-generation Portuguese monolingual encoder using ModernBERT architecture and trained on 106 million documents, outperforming previous models in NLP tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed BERTomelo, a new Portuguese monolingual encoder built on the ModernBERT architecture and trained from scratch on a large corpus of 106 million Portuguese documents. This model offers Base and Large versions with enhanced context windows and hardware optimizations, outperforming previous Portuguese encoders like BERTimbau and Albertina in natural language processing tasks such as semantic textual similarity and named entity recognition. BERTomelo addresses the limitations of earlier models by incorporating recent architectural advances and aligning closely with contemporary Portuguese usage. Its design includes features like FlashAttention and alternating attention mechanisms, which contribute to improved scalability and efficiency compared to both prior monolingual models and large multilingual alternatives. The introduction of BERTomelo represents a significant step forward in Portuguese language processing, providing a more robust and efficient tool for various NLP applications. Its superior performance suggests potential for broader adoption in tasks requiring deep contextual understanding of Portuguese text.

entry.title: Researchers analyze distributional gap between synthetic and real speech in LLM-based ASR systems and propose RIR augmentation with layer selection to match real-data performance using 25% real speech [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have investigated the distributional differences between synthetic and real speech in large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems, particularly in privacy-sensitive domains like banking and healthcare where real speech data is limited. They identified that the early-to-middle layers of the LLM backbone are key in distinguishing synthetic from real speech, with temporal and prosodic variations playing a significant role. By applying room impulse response (RIR) augmentation to synthetic audio and incorporating a layer-selection module during training, they achieved ASR performance comparable to models trained on fully real data using only 25% of real speech, and surpassed it with higher proportions of real data.

entry.title: Researchers present AB-RAG, an adaptive, training-free retrieval-augmented generation framework that estimates answer confidence and adjusts retrieval budget for reliable question answering across multiple language model backbones [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced AB-RAG, an adaptive, training-free framework for retrieval-augmented generation that enhances question answering by estimating answer confidence and dynamically adjusting the retrieval budget. Unlike traditional systems that retrieve a fixed number of passages regardless of question difficulty, AB-RAG uses a combination of signals-including model certainty, answer-evidence agreement, and retrieval score variance-to decide when to stop or continue retrieving information, improving reliability without retraining the underlying language model. The framework is backbone-agnostic and works with both open models that expose token probabilities and closed APIs by approximating confidence through self-consistency. Evaluations across three language model backbones and two datasets demonstrated that AB-RAG effectively distinguishes correct from incorrect answers, significantly improving accuracy on capable models. The study also transparently reports limitations and adjustments made during development, all conducted efficiently on a consumer laptop with minimal API costs.

entry.title: Researchers establish a formal barrier for tabular foundation models showing they cannot distinguish rule-violating from legal database states without operational grounding, despite access to schema and data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have demonstrated a formal limitation for tabular foundation models, showing that these models cannot reliably distinguish between rule-compliant and rule-violating database states without access to the operational rules governing the data. Using the Operational Turing Test (OTT), they created pairs of database states with nearly identical statistical properties, proving that classifiers relying solely on data values perform no better than random guessing. Only models incorporating executable rule-based audits achieved perfect classification accuracy. The study tested various baseline models, including XGBoost and large language models like GPT-5.5, which failed to correctly identify legal states even when provided with schema, triggers, and rule tables. This limitation was consistent across different database schemas and rule types, indicating that the barrier arises from identifiability issues rather than model capacity or data scale. These findings imply that without operational grounding-explicit knowledge of the rules that generate data-tabular foundation models cannot effectively reason about dynamic, rule-governed systems. This highlights the necessity of integrating rule-based information to improve model reliability in applications involving complex database states.

entry.title: Researchers develop normal-fan geometry for finite-horizon adversarial MDPs to analyze dynamic regret and non-stationarity costs through priced face-crossing motion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new geometric framework called normal-fan geometry to analyze dynamic regret and non-stationarity costs in finite-horizon adversarial Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) with fixed transitions. This approach models occupancy measures as a polytope where each loss vector corresponds to an optimal face, allowing the study of how changes in rewards affect the optimal policy through movements within and across these faces. The concept of a face-crossing price quantifies the minimum regret incurred when the optimal policy changes due to shifts in the loss function. This framework distinguishes between harmless and consequential non-stationarity by showing that large variations in loss can occur without increasing regret if the optimal face remains the same, while even small changes crossing a face boundary can lead to significant regret. The theory decomposes dynamic regret into intrinsic costs associated with moving between optimal faces and errors within a face, providing a more precise understanding of the impact of non-stationarity on learning performance in adversarial MDPs.

entry.title: Researchers introduce BTI-Net with bidirectional decoder-level task interaction and uncertainty-aware gating, improving segmentation and classification accuracy on ultrasound, dermoscopy, and brain MRI benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed BTI-Net, a novel multi-task learning framework that enhances medical image segmentation and classification by enabling bidirectional interaction between decoder branches. Unlike traditional encoder-sharing models that limit cross-task information exchange, BTI-Net uses Task Interaction Modules to integrate spatial boundary cues and global semantic priors at every decoder level, improving feature refinement from coarse to fine details. The model also incorporates Uncertainty Proxy Attention to adaptively gate interactions based on cross-task alignment, scene complexity, and prediction confidence without extra annotations or inference steps. Evaluations on ultrasound, dermoscopy, and brain MRI datasets demonstrate that BTI-Net consistently outperforms existing encoder-sharing and decoder-interaction baselines, achieving notable gains in segmentation intersection-over-union and classification accuracy. Ablation studies confirm that the adaptive gating mechanism significantly contributes to performance improvements, and the uncertainty proxies effectively signal task failures in a single pass, reducing computational overhead. The researchers have made the code publicly available for further exploration and application.

entry.title: Researchers introduce a pre-registered screening rule to predict when evolutionary outer loops over neural network parameters are not cost-effective, validated with 6-8x GPU-hour savings [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a pre-registered screening rule to determine in advance whether implementing an evolutionary outer loop over neural network parameters or structure is cost-effective. This rule calculates a recovery ratio based on gradient and curvature statistics and recommends skipping the outer loop if the ratio exceeds 90%, potentially saving significant computational resources. The approach was validated through multiple cases within a lab, where it successfully identified scenarios where the outer loop provided no substantial benefit, leading to substantial GPU-hour savings and reduced implementation time. The screening rule operates at an initial phase, computing a single metric that compares the best single-shot method's gain to that of any cheap alternative. In tested cases, the rule accurately predicted when the evolutionary outer loop would not outperform simpler methods, allowing researchers to avoid costly computations. One example demonstrated a 6-8 times reduction in GPU hours by applying the rule, highlighting its practical efficiency. This method is designed to be prospectively falsifiable, meaning it can be tested and potentially disproven if future tasks with a recovery ratio below 90% fail to benefit from the outer loop. The rule offers a systematic way to assess the value of complex evolutionary strategies before committing extensive resources, which could influence future neural network optimization practices.

entry.title: Researchers find anthropomorphic language has modest immediate effects on public perceptions of AI across large language models and recommendation systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A recent study examined how anthropomorphic language-attributing human traits to artificial intelligence (AI)-affects public perceptions of AI technologies, including large language models and recommendation systems. Researchers compared participants' views after reading passages with and without anthropomorphic language and found that such language has only modest immediate effects on how people perceive AI. The study also showed that explicit discussions about AI dangers can shift opinions, but the use of anthropomorphic descriptions alone does not significantly alter perceptions. The research involved 815 participants and aimed to reflect realistic public discourse about AI. While the immediate impact of anthropomorphic language was limited, the study suggests that longer-term or naturalistic exposure might produce different effects. These findings contribute to understanding how language influences public understanding and policy discussions surrounding AI.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Generative Pretrained Controllers using large-scale motion datasets and GPT-style transformers for robust, transferable motor control with 99.98% success in motion reproduction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Generative Pretrained Controllers (GPC), a novel approach that uses large-scale motion datasets and GPT-style transformers to create versatile, reusable controllers for physics-based character animation. This method combines reinforcement learning with a learned motion vocabulary and an autoregressive transformer to generate precise motor controls, achieving a 99.98% success rate in reproducing diverse motion clips. The framework simplifies training compared to previous tokenized methods by jointly optimizing a discrete motion codebook and a control policy. The resulting generative controller demonstrates natural behaviors such as responding to perturbations and recovering from falls, making it highly robust and adaptable for various downstream tasks through fine-tuning techniques. This advancement offers a powerful tool for creating lifelike, general-purpose motor control in simulated characters, potentially enhancing applications in animation, robotics, and interactive environments.

entry.title: Researchers find optimal learning rate scaling for GPT-2 models deviates from log-linear law at large scales, with effective learning rate and data extrapolation reducing nonlinearity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have investigated the scaling of optimal learning rates for training GPT-2 models and found that the commonly assumed log-linear scaling law does not hold at larger model and data scales. Their study, covering models from 22 million to 707 million parameters trained on 5 billion to 100 billion tokens, revealed an upward curvature in the optimal learning rate that leads to inaccurate extrapolations when using traditional methods. The team discovered that this nonlinearity largely disappears when using the effective learning rate, defined as the step size in normalized weight space, and when extrapolating based on data scale rather than model size. They attribute the nonlinearity to slower convergence of weight norms at smaller optimal learning rates, which necessitates larger step sizes to reduce transient training phases. Experiments with the AdamH optimizer, which directly controls effective learning rate, supported these findings, offering insights that could improve learning rate transfer and reduce training costs for large language models.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Trajectory-Invariant Latent Refinement (TILR) to identify stable reasoning directions in language model latent trajectories, improving consistency and reducing variance across six benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed Trajectory-Invariant Latent Refinement (TILR), a new framework designed to identify and manipulate stable reasoning directions within the latent trajectories of language models. This approach addresses the challenge of variability in latent reasoning paths caused by paraphrases, model checkpoints, and perturbations, by focusing on a low-rank invariant subspace that captures consistent reasoning behavior. TILR improves reasoning consistency and reduces variance across six benchmarks without requiring additional training. TILR operates by learning a low-dimensional subspace from differences between stronger and weaker reasoning trajectories and constrains latent updates to this subspace while filtering out unstable variations. Experiments show that a small number of latent directions explain most of the variation in reasoning quality, and interventions along these directions enhance answer consistency by about 10% and reduce trajectory variance by up to 50%, all while maintaining reasoning accuracy. These findings support a geometric perspective on latent reasoning, suggesting that transferable reasoning capabilities emerge from stable, low-dimensional structures within hidden-state trajectories. This insight could inform future improvements in the robustness and interpretability of language model reasoning processes.

entry.title: Researchers present a hybrid human-LLM framework for song lyric annotation to address emotion recognition challenges and predict annotation misalignment [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a hybrid framework combining human input and large language models (LLMs) to improve the annotation of song lyrics for emotion recognition, addressing the challenge that lyrics may not always reflect a song's overall emotion. They created a new sentence-level dataset to study the alignment between human annotators and LLMs, revealing the subjective nature of this task and its inherent difficulties.
