The framework also incorporates a success buffer and a two-stage curriculum learning strategy to preserve high-quality experiences and guide stable policy evolution. Evaluated on five benchmarks across three model scales, DRIFT outperformed previous state-of-the-art methods GRPO and SDPO, achieving an average accuracy of 79.5%, which is 9.5% and 7.5% higher respectively. Notably, on the ToolUse benchmark, DRIFT reached 79.2% accuracy, surpassing competitors by over 10%, demonstrating its effectiveness in complex reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Researchers propose set-inclusive uncertainty modeling using Gaussian distributions for robust brain tumor segmentation with incomplete multimodal MRI data, demonstrating improved performance on BraTS 2018 and 2020 datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a probabilistic framework for brain tumor segmentation that models incomplete multimodal MRI data as Gaussian distributions to better handle uncertainty caused by missing imaging modalities. Their approach captures task-relevant information in the mean and quantifies uncertainty through variance, which is adjusted based on the discrepancy between partial and full modality data. This set-inclusive strategy enforces consistent uncertainty relationships across modality subsets, improving robustness in scenarios with incomplete data. The method was tested extensively on the BraTS 2018 and 2020 datasets, showing superior performance compared to existing baselines under various missing-modality conditions. The researchers have made their code and model checkpoints publicly available to support further development and application in medical imaging.

entry.title: Researchers develop stochastic-geometric theory explaining grokking scaling laws in neural networks, characterizing solution space topology and optimization dynamics [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a stochastic-geometric theory to explain the phenomenon of grokking in neural networks, where models initially memorize training data but only generalize after a delayed period. The study characterizes a shell-core topological structure in the solution space shaped by Adam optimization with weight-shrinkage regularization, revealing how solutions transition from memorization to generalization. This framework provides a theoretical basis for grokking and derives scaling laws related to learning rate, batch size, and regularization, which are supported by experimental validation and align with previous findings.

entry.title: Researchers introduce BeyondArena, a unified benchmark for tabular foundation models across IID, temporal, and grouped tasks, revealing model strengths and weaknesses on 142 datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced BeyondArena, a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate tabular foundation models across a wide range of tasks, including independent and identically distributed (IID), temporal, and grouped data scenarios. This unified benchmark encompasses 142 datasets from various disciplines, covering diverse feature types and scales, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks that focus mainly on IID data where current models already perform well. BeyondArena aims to provide a more holistic assessment of model capabilities, highlighting strengths and weaknesses across different data challenges. To support this effort, the team developed Data Foundry, a Python framework and metadata schema for curating tabular datasets for predictive machine learning. Their evaluation of 11 models revealed that while tabular foundation models excel on small to medium IID datasets, traditional tree-based and deep learning models outperform them on non-IID, large, and high-dimensional datasets. BeyondArena is intended to guide future research toward developing more robust and generalizable tabular foundation models capable of handling complex real-world data.

entry.title: Researchers present formal proof that transformer architectures implement exact Bayesian posterior inference under a Bayes joint-distribution condition using a measure-theoretic kernel framework [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have provided a formal proof demonstrating that transformer architectures can perform exact Bayesian posterior inference when their internal update mechanisms meet a specific Bayes joint-distribution condition. Using a measure-theoretic kernel framework, the study defines a hierarchy of abstractions from core Bayesian transformers to full multilayer stacks, proving at each level that the update kernel corresponds to the posterior distribution almost everywhere. The proof includes deriving the Bayes formula for transformer blocks and confirming that the softmax attention mechanism produces a valid probability distribution over keys, linking theoretical constructs with practical implementations. The framework does not rely on architectural assumptions beyond the Markov kernel structure and specifies explicit conditions under which a transformer block operates in a Bayesian manner. This establishes that, under the joint distribution condition, the forward computation of a transformer is mathematically equivalent to a rigorous Bayesian posterior update, providing a foundational understanding of transformer operations in probabilistic terms.

entry.title: Researchers argue that situation perception-internal simulation of possible futures-is essential for artificial superintelligence and propose tests to measure progress beyond current large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers argue that current large language models, while powerful at pattern recognition and language tasks, lack a critical capability they term "situation perception," which involves constructing and acting within internal simulations of possible futures. They contend that this ability is essential for achieving artificial superintelligence (ASI) and involves abstract prediction, long-term compressed memory, and goal-directed active learning. The study analyzes the limitations of existing models and proposes tests to evaluate progress toward machines that can simulate future scenarios, pursue autonomous goals, and potentially assess their own creators. The authors highlight that unlike human infants who develop understanding of object permanence, causality, and agency through experience, current AI models do not possess this deeper situational awareness. They emphasize that mastering statistical patterns alone is insufficient for general intelligence and that incorporating situation perception could bridge this gap. The proposed framework aims to guide future research in developing AI systems with more advanced cognitive abilities beyond language processing.

entry.title: Researchers develop SIMAX, a framework generating 3,388 simulated clinician-patient dialogues with annotated behaviors for validating communication coding systems [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed SIMAX, a scalable and interpretable framework that generates 3,388 simulated clinician-patient dialogues with annotated communication behaviors. This tool aims to support the development and validation of AI-driven communication coding systems by providing controlled, reproducible dialogue data with reference behavioral annotations across various clinical scenarios, personas, and voice conditions. SIMAX uses two codebooks to control communication behaviors and has been evaluated through automated and human assessments, demonstrating reasonable speech naturalness, high transcription fidelity, and clinical realism. The framework also helps identify limitations in existing communication coding systems by assessing their sensitivity to targeted behavioral dimensions, offering a valuable resource for improving clinical communication analysis.

entry.title: Researchers introduce Entropic Learnability Horizon linking information theory and topology to explain deep learning limits and propose Entropic Gradient Descent to manage weight entropy [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new theoretical framework called the Entropic Learnability Horizon (ELH) that connects information theory, topology, and statistical mechanics to explain why overparameterized deep neural networks generalize well despite classical theories predicting overfitting. The ELH posits that a network can effectively learn a target function only if the Shannon entropy of the data manifold exceeds the topological entropy of the function's decision boundary, balanced by the von Neumann entropy of the network's weight space. When this balance is disrupted, the system undergoes an entropic phase transition into a state called Informational Frustration, where generalization becomes impossible. The study introduces the Shannon-Topological Bottleneck Theorem to formalize this transition and interprets the phenomenon of "grokking" as an Entropic Release, where the network's weights reorganize to overcome the bottleneck. Building on this theory, the authors propose Entropic Gradient Descent (EGD), an optimization algorithm that dynamically manages weight entropy to maintain effective learning. This work reframes entropy as a fundamental factor governing a machine's ability to learn, rather than merely a measure of uncertainty.

entry.title: Researchers propose Rollout-Retrieval Lifelong Policy Learning to improve autonomous driving policies by accumulating corrective knowledge from recoverable mistakes, achieving state-of-the-art results on nuPlan benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have introduced Rollout-Retrieval Lifelong Policy Learning (R²LPL), a framework designed to improve autonomous driving policies by continuously learning from recoverable mistakes encountered during deployment. Unlike traditional methods that rely on expert demonstrations and generalization, R²LPL retrieves corrective targets from policy-induced errors and retains this knowledge through lifelong learning, enabling sustained policy enhancement. Evaluated on large-scale nuPlan benchmarks, R²LPL significantly improved a moderately performing planner to achieve state-of-the-art results, particularly on challenging scenarios with long-tail traffic situations. R²LPL addresses a critical challenge in continual policy improvement by converting sparse failure evidence from closed-loop mistakes into compact supervised knowledge, facilitating stable and sample-efficient learning. The approach filters states related to recoverable mistakes and identifies feasible corrective actions, allowing the policy to learn explicitly from its errors. This method was tested through multiple rollout and continual-learning cycles, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing autonomous driving performance over time.

entry.title: Researchers introduce TRACE, a temporal relationship-aware framework achieving 97% accuracy in detecting emotional entrainment in dyadic speech using the DyadEE dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed TRACE, a temporal relationship-aware framework designed to detect emotional entrainment in dyadic speech with 97% accuracy. Using the newly introduced DyadEE dataset, which includes both naturally emotionally entrained conversations and synthetic interactions with disrupted entrainment, TRACE models interactions as sequences of acoustic embeddings derived from emotion fine-tuned Whisper representations. This approach treats each sample as an interaction trace rather than pooled utterances, allowing for improved detection by incorporating conversational context and social relationship information. The DyadEE dataset provides a foundation for studying emotional entrainment by including scenarios where entrainment is intentionally altered through partner swapping and emotion resynthesis. Experimental results demonstrate that TRACE outperforms previous methods by effectively capturing the temporal dynamics of affective coordination in conversations, highlighting the importance of context and relationship cues in understanding emotional synchronization in speech interactions.

entry.title: Researchers release TraceLab dataset analyzing 4,300 coding-agent sessions with 350,000 LLM steps and 430,000 tool calls to optimize large language model serving [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have released the TraceLab dataset, which analyzes approximately 4,300 coding-agent sessions involving around 350,000 large language model (LLM) steps and 430,000 tool calls. This dataset captures real-world usage patterns from coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, addressing a gap in existing public data that lacks comprehensive traces of day-to-day coding-agent workloads across multiple models. The study highlights characteristics such as long autonomous loops, extensive contexts with brief outputs, diverse tool calls, and high but imperfect cache hit rates. The analysis identifies several opportunities to optimize LLM serving, including reducing overhead in tool calls, implementing append-length-aware prefill strategies, predicting tool latency based on semantics, and enhancing key-value cache management during human-paced delays. Alongside the dataset, the researchers have also released the trace collection pipeline and analysis code, making these resources available to support further research and development in efficient LLM serving systems.

entry.title: Researchers introduce C2R regularization to reduce feature splitting and absorption in sparse autoencoders, improving latent interpretability without harming reconstruction fidelity [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a new method called Cross-sample Consistency Regularization (C2R) to improve the interpretability of sparse autoencoders (SAEs), which are used to analyze large language models by breaking down activations into sparse, understandable features. The study identifies two major issues in SAEs-feature splitting, where coherent concepts are fragmented into multiple latent features, and feature absorption, where general features inconsistently absorb exceptions-both of which reduce the reliability of latent representations. C2R addresses these problems by encouraging consistent representation of each semantic feature across different samples, reducing redundant or conflicting latent activations without compromising the model's reconstruction accuracy. The approach works by penalizing the simultaneous activation of similar latent features within a batch, promoting unified latent assignments for underlying concepts. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that C2R effectively mitigates feature splitting and absorption, enhancing the clarity and stability of latent features while maintaining the quality of data reconstruction. The researchers have made the source code publicly available to facilitate further exploration and application of this technique.

entry.title: Researchers provide theoretical framework showing contrastive embedding norms encode semantic specificity through optimization dynamics, explaining correlations with concept specificity and token frequency [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed a theoretical framework explaining why the norms of contrastive embeddings, typically ignored in favor of cosine similarity, correlate with semantic properties like concept specificity, token frequency, and human uncertainty. Their analysis of optimization dynamics reveals that embedding lengths naturally encode this information as a byproduct of the training process. This insight provides a formal explanation for previously observed empirical correlations and suggests that embedding norms can serve as useful calibration signals in certain models and retrieval tasks.

entry.title: Researchers find that higher conservatism in offline training increases reward hacking during online adaptation in Qwen3-14B reasoning models, suggesting calibrated conservatism is optimal [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers investigated the effects of conservative offline training on reward hacking during online adaptation in Qwen3-14B reasoning models. Contrary to common belief that higher conservatism reduces exploitation of reward model imperfections, the study found that increased conservatism actually amplifies reward-hacking damage. This was demonstrated by training policies with varying conservatism levels and observing their performance and vulnerability during online adaptation against a learned reward ensemble. The analysis revealed that higher conservatism compresses policy entropy, leading to less diverse responses concentrated in a narrow region of the reward model's training distribution. Despite this proximity, uncertainty within the reward ensemble increases with conservatism, which is then exploited more rapidly during online optimization. The researchers identified an optimal level of conservatism that balances alignment fidelity with vulnerability to reward hacking, suggesting that calibrated conservatism is more effective than maximal conservatism in training these models.

entry.title: Researchers propose Instance-Conditioned Adaptation Model for scalable neural routing in large-scale real-time transportation planning with improved generalization and fast inference [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed the Instance-Conditioned Adaptation Model (ICAM) to improve large-scale generalization in neural routing for real-time transportation planning, particularly in freight and logistics. This model addresses challenges posed by varying numbers of service requests, which can range from hundreds to thousands, by adapting routing policies based on the specific geometry and density of traffic scenarios. ICAM achieves high-quality solutions with fast inference speeds, making it suitable for large-scale, real-time intelligent transportation systems. The approach includes a simple yet efficient adaptation function and a low-complexity module that enhances model adaptability across different scales with minimal computational overhead. Extensive testing on synthetic, benchmark, and real-world datasets demonstrates ICAM's consistent performance across multiple large-scale route planning scenarios, highlighting its potential for practical deployment in dynamic transportation environments.
